jobs.title: VP Hospital Health System ISC Managed Service Business Development Growth & Ente
jobs.excerpt: When you’re the best, we’re the best.  We instill an environment where employees feel engaged, satisfied and able to contribute their unique skills and talents while living and working as their authentic selves.
jobs.description:
When you’re the best, we’re the best. We instill an environment where employees feel engaged, satisfied and able to contribute their unique skills and talents while living and working as their authentic selves. We provide extensive opportunities for personal and professional development, building both employee competence and organizational capability to fuel exceptional performance through an inclusive environment both now and in the future.

Your Role at Vizient:

Vizient provides purchasing power and data/analytics to US hospital healthcare systems improve margins, resilience and availability of supplies. In addition, Vizient offers operational expertise and managed service as part of the Spend Management business unit. As the VP, ISC Growth & Enterprise Solutions, you will be responsible for accelerating growth of Vizient’s Integrated Supply Chain business by translating client needs and market opportunities into differentiated, executable, and financially sustainable enterprise solutions.

You will serve as the primary ISC partner to Sales and business development teams, leading solution architecture for complex health systems, IDNs, and strategic prospects. You will bring together client needs, Vizient capabilities, subject matter expertise, financial modeling, staffing requirements, implementation considerations, and value propositions into an integrated solution designed to deliver measurable client outcomes.

Operating within a highly matrixed environment, orchestrating resources across Integrated Supply Chain, National Centers, Sales, Finance, Human Resources, Legal, Analytics, and other enterprise functions, you won’t need to directly own every capability required to develop a solution; rather, you’ll be accountable for ensuring the right expertise is engaged, decisions are made, assumptions are validated, and the resulting model is operationally achievable and commercially compelling.

Reporting to the SVP Spend Management Solutions, you will initially operate as a senior player-coach and enterprise integrator, personally leading major pursuits and solution design while leveraging resources from across the organization. As the ISC business scales, you will build and lead a dedicated enterprise solutions capability, including solution architecture and other growth-enablement resources as business demand warrants.

As the VP ISC Growth & Solution Strategy, you will serve as the bridge between business development and operational delivery, ensuring that what Vizient sells can be successfully implemented, scaled, and sustained. You’ll partner closely with the VP, Transformation & Practice and client-facing Integrated Supply Chain leaders to create a disciplined handoff from pursuit through implementation.

Success in this role requires the ability to understand hospital health system complex client environments, create clarity from ambiguity, lead through influence, develop innovative commercial solutions, and balance growth with operational feasibility, financial performance, and long-term client value.

What You’ll Be Doing:

Growth Strategy & Business Development

  • Serve as the senior Integrated Supply Chain leader supporting Sales and business development efforts for new Integrated Supply Chain opportunities.
  • Partner with Sales leadership to develop and execute growth strategies that expand the Integrated Supply Chain business.
  • Engage with prospective client executives to understand strategic priorities, business challenges, organizational dynamics, performance opportunities, and transformation objectives.
  • Provide supply chain executive credibility and subject matter expertise throughout the pursuit process.
  • Assess and prioritize opportunities based on strategic fit, client need, organizational readiness, revenue potential, complexity, and probability of success.
  • Support development of pipeline strategy, pursuit priorities, and resource allocation across active opportunities.
  • Participate in executive-level client presentations, discovery sessions, proposal discussions, and final-stage negotiations.
  • Identify emerging market needs and translate them into new Integrated Supply Chain offerings and growth opportunities.
  • Build relationships across Vizient to ensure Integrated Supply Chain is appropriately represented within enterprise growth initiatives.

Enterprise Solution Architecture

  • Lead the development of integrated supply chain solutions for prospective and expanding clients.
  • Translate discovery findings into clearly defined service models, scope, organizational structures, staffing models, governance, performance expectations, and transformation roadmaps.
  • Ensure solutions appropriately integrate sourcing, value analysis, analytics, inventory management, purchasing, operations, and other relevant Vizient capabilities.
  • Define which capabilities should be embedded within the client engagement versus deployed through enterprise or National Center resources.
  • Design solutions that balance client-specific needs with standardized, repeatable Integrated Supply Chain operating models.
  • Minimize unnecessary customization while ensuring the solution addresses the client’s most important strategic and operational needs.
  • Develop clear assumptions, dependencies, risks, and decision points associated with proposed operating models.
  • Partner with the VP, Transformation & Practice to ensure proposed solutions can be effectively transitioned, implemented, and scaled.

Financial, Staffing & Commercial Modeling

  • Lead development of staffing and resource models required to support proposed Integrated Supply Chain solutions.
  • Partner with Finance, Human Resources, Sales, and operational leaders to develop sustainable financial and commercial models.
  • Evaluate labor requirements, shared-service opportunities, enterprise support needs, implementation requirements, and other cost drivers.
  • Ensure proposed solutions balance competitive pricing, client value, delivery requirements, and appropriate margin performance.
  • Develop business cases that articulate expected client outcomes, value creation, required investment, and financial impact.
  • Challenge assumptions and identify opportunities to improve solution economics without compromising client outcomes.
  • Ensure financial and staffing assumptions are clearly documented and transferred to implementation and delivery leaders following contract execution.

Pursuit Leadership & Sales Enablement

  • Establish a disciplined Integrated Supply Chain pursuit process from initial opportunity identification through contract handoff.
  • Coordinate subject matter experts and enterprise resources required to support discovery, solution development, proposals, presentations, and due diligence.
  • Ensure pursuit teams operate with clear roles, timelines, deliverables, decision rights, and accountability.
  • Develop reusable proposal content, solution frameworks, discovery tools, staffing methodologies, executive presentations, and supporting materials.
  • Partner with Sales to strengthen positioning and articulation of the Integrated Supply Chain value proposition.
  • Develop repeatable tools and processes that reduce dependence on individual leaders and accelerate response time for new opportunities.
  • Capture lessons learned from pursuits and continuously improve the business development and solutioning process.

Transition Readiness & Operational Handoff

  • Ensure contracted solutions are transitioned to delivery teams with clear documentation of scope, commitments, assumptions, staffing, financial expectations, and client priorities.
  • Partner with the VP, Transformation & Practice to initiate the appropriate implementation structure immediately following contract execution.
  • Participate in formal handoff sessions with the assigned client VP, implementation leadership, analytics, and other enterprise teams.
  • Ensure commitments made during the sales process are understood and operationally achievable.
  • Remain engaged during early implementation when clarification of solution intent, scope, or commercial assumptions is required.
  • Establish feedback loops between delivery and solution development so future pursuits benefit from actual implementation experience.

Enterprise Offering & Capability Development

  • Identify patterns across client opportunities that can be translated into standardized services, offerings, tools, or commercial models.
  • Partner with the VP, Transformation & Practice and ISC Strategy & Business Architecture leadership to develop repeatable Integrated Supply Chain offerings.
  • Identify capability gaps that may limit growth and develop recommendations to build, buy, partner, or leverage existing Vizient resources.
  • Maintain an enterprise view of the Integrated Supply Chain service portfolio and ensure offerings remain aligned with market demand.
  • Incorporate client success stories, benchmarks, transformation outcomes, and demonstrated value into future growth efforts.
  • Support development of strategic partnerships that enhance Vizient’s ability to deliver differentiated client solutions.

Matrix Leadership & Alignment

  • Lead complex cross-functional pursuits without direct authority over all participating resources.
  • Create clarity, structure, decision discipline, and accountability across Sales, National Centers, Integrated Supply Chain, and other enterprise stakeholders.
  • Establish clear roles and responsibilities during solution development and pursuit execution.
  • Build strong working relationships with National Center and enterprise leaders to ensure expertise can be rapidly mobilized for opportunities.
  • Resolve competing priorities and escalate decisions when necessary to maintain pursuit momentum.
  • Balance speed to market with appropriate diligence, financial discipline, and operational feasibility.
  • Foster an enterprise-first mindset that prioritizes the best integrated solution for the client rather than individual functional interests.

Leadership & Talent Development

  • Build the future Enterprise Solutions capability as Integrated Supply Chain growth creates sufficient demand.
  • Develop solution architecture and growth-enablement talent capable of independently leading increasingly complex opportunities.
  • Coach subject matter experts and emerging leaders on executive discovery, solution development, commercial thinking, and client presentation skills.
  • Create repeatable processes and delegation models that reduce key-person dependency.
  • Develop succession plans and organizational capacity necessary to support continued business growth.

Enterprise Leadership

  • Serve as an enterprise leader within the Integrated Supply Chain organization, contributing to strategy and priorities beyond individual pursuits.
  • Partner closely with client VPs, VP/GMs, the VP, Transformation & Practice, and National Center leadership to align growth with delivery capability.
  • Provide market intelligence and pipeline insights that inform workforce planning, capability investment, and organizational strategy.
  • Support the evolution and scalability of Vizient’s Integrated Supply Chain model.
  • Balance near-term revenue growth with long-term client success, financial sustainability, and enterprise scalability.

Your Location:

The role is located at our corporate headquarters in Irving, TX or our facilities in Chicago, IL or Centennial, CO. Remote work within the United States will also be considered.

What You’ll Bring:

  • Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree preferred.
  • Business Development Growth mindset and able to travel 50%+.

  • 10+ years of progressive leadership experience in healthcare supply chain, healthcare consulting, business development, solution architecture, hospital operations, or related fields.
  • Demonstrated experience designing complex operating models, managed services, outsourced services, consulting solutions, or large-scale transformation programs.
  • Strong understanding of healthcare supply chain functions, including sourcing, value analysis, analytics, inventory management, purchasing, and operations.
  • Proven ability to engage and influence executive-level stakeholders within complex health systems or similarly complex organizations.
  • Demonstrated commercial and financial acumen, including experience with staffing models, business cases, pricing assumptions, and solution economics.
  • Proven success operating in highly matrixed organizations and mobilizing cross-functional teams without direct authority.
  • Strong executive communication, facilitation, presentation, and negotiation skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate ambiguous client needs into structured, executable solutions.
  • Experience supporting complex sales pursuits, proposals, RFPs, or strategic client expansion opportunities strongly preferred.

Estimated Hiring Range:

At Vizient, we consider skills, experience, and organizational needs in our compensation approach. Geographic factors may adjust the range estimate and hires typically fall below the top range. Compensation decisions are tailored to individual circumstances. The current salary range for this role is $187,800.00 to $348,300.00.

This position is also incentive eligible.

Our ideal Clinical Guide is detail-oriented, solutions-focused, and comfortable making well-documented clinical judgments at pace. You’re someone who can hold accuracy and volume at the same time, and who is energized rather than unsettled by evolving policies and workflows.

jobs.excerpt: By joining Sedgwick, you'll be part of something truly meaningful.
jobs.description:
By joining Sedgwick, you'll be part of something truly meaningful. It’s what our 33,000 colleagues do every day for people around the world who are facing the unexpected. We invite you to grow your career with us, experience our caring culture, and enjoy work-life balance. Here, there’s no limit to what you can achieve.

Newsweek Recognizes Sedgwick as America’s Greatest Workplaces National Top Companies

Certified as a Great Place to Work®

Fortune Best Workplaces in Financial Services & Insurance

Application Developer - Security Engineering

PRIMARY PURPOSE

Designs, develops, and maintains applications, integrations, and automation that support enterprise security operations. Partners with Security Operations, IAM, Cloud Engineering, and Enterprise Architecture to turn detection and response requirements into working software. Builds and tunes content within the organization’s SIEM platform, develops data pipelines that feed it, and automates response workflows. Applies secure-by-default engineering practices, least privilege, and documented change control to everything delivered.


Essential Functions and Responsibilities


Application development

  • Develops, tests, and maintains applications, APIs, and services supporting security operations and compliance reporting.
  • Writes code that follows secure development standards, including input validation, output encoding, secrets management through an approved vault, and dependency scanning in the build pipeline.
  • Participates in peer code review, maintains unit and integration test coverage, and supports CI/CD pipelines for application and detection content releases.
  • Produces and maintains technical documentation, including design decisions, data flows, interface contracts, and runbooks with named ownership.

SIEM engineering and detection content

  • Builds, tests, and tunes SIEM detection rules, correlation searches, dashboards, and scheduled reports.
  • Develops and maintains log ingestion pipelines: source onboarding, parsing, field extraction, normalization to a common schema, and enrichment.
  • Troubleshoots ingestion gaps, parsing failures, licensing and volume issues, and data quality problems affecting detection reliability.
  • Manages detection content as code in version control, with documented test cases, promotion through non-production environments, and rollback procedures.
  • Maps detection coverage to a recognized framework such as MITRE ATT&CK and reports coverage gaps to Security leadership.

Automation and integration

  • Develops integrations between the SIEM and adjacent platforms, including EDR, identity, ticketing, vulnerability management, and cloud-native security services.
  • Builds SOAR playbooks and automation scripts that reduce manual analyst effort, with approval gates on any action that is destructive or privileged.
  • Instruments applications and infrastructure for security-relevant logging and validates that required audit events reach the SIEM.

Governance and collaboration

  • Works with Security, Cloud Engineering, IAM, and application teams to gather requirements and validate that delivered tooling meets operational need.
  • Supports audit and compliance evidence requests related to logging, monitoring, and alerting controls.
  • Follows enterprise change management for all production changes, including approvals, testing evidence, and defined back-out plans.
  • Participates in an on-call or escalation rotation for critical security tooling.

Qualifications


  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Cybersecurity, or a related field; equivalent combination of education and experience considered.
  • Four or more years of professional software development experience.
  • Two or more years working directly with a SIEM platform, Google Security Operations (Google SecOps) preferred; comparable experience with Microsoft Sentinel, Splunk, Elastic Security, or IBM QRadar considered.
  • Proficiency writing SIEM query and detection logic — for example YARA-L 2.0 in Google SecOps, or KQL, SPL, or an equivalent query language — including performance tuning of scheduled rules and searches.
  • Strong programming skills in at least one of Python, C#/.NET, Java, or Go, plus scripting with PowerShell or Bash.
  • Working knowledge of REST API development and consumption, JSON, authentication patterns including OAuth 2.0, and webhook-based integration.
  • Experience with Git-based version control and CI/CD pipelines.
  • Practical understanding of core security concepts: authentication and authorization, encryption in transit and at-rest, logging and audit requirements, least privilege, and common attack techniques.
  • Demonstrated ability to document assumptions, dependencies, and operational ownership for delivered work.

Preferred qualifications


  • Hands-on Google SecOps engineering experience, including UDM (Unified Data Model) normalization, parser and parser-extension development, log forwarder and ingestion API onboarding, data RBAC, reference lists, and Applied Threat Intelligence or curated detection content.
  • Experience with log pipeline and routing tools such as Cribl, Logstash, Fluent Bit, or Kafka.
  • Detection-as-code practices, including Sigma rules, automated detection testing, and content promotion pipelines.
  • SOAR development experience, Google SecOps SOAR (formerly Siemplify) preferred; Microsoft Sentinel playbooks, Splunk SOAR, or Cortex XSOAR also considered. Includes playbook design, custom integration and action development in Python, and case management workflow configuration.
  • Cloud security engineering in Azure or AWS, including native logging services, managed identities, and private networking patterns; working familiarity with Google Cloud a plus given the SecOps platform.
  • Infrastructure as code with Terraform or Bicep.
  • Experience supporting regulated data environments and control frameworks such as SOC 2, HIPAA, PCI DSS, SOX, or NIST CSF.
  • Relevant certifications, for example Google Cloud Professional Security Engineer, Google SecOps platform training or credentials, Microsoft SC-200, GIAC GCDA or GCIA, CompTIA Security+, or CISSP.
  • Experience with containerized workloads and Kubernetes.

Core Competencies

  • Translates security requirements into maintainable software rather than one-off scripts.
  • Communicates technical risk clearly to operations, engineering, and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Exercises judgment about blast radius before acting on production systems.
  • Works effectively across security, infrastructure, and application teams with competing priorities.
  • Maintains confidentiality when handling sensitive security, customer, or employee data.

Work environment

· When applicable and appropriate, consideration will be given to reasonable accommodation.

· Mental: Clear and conceptual thinking ability; excellent judgment, troubleshooting, problem solving, analysis, and discretion; ability to handle work-related stress; ability to handle multiple priorities simultaneously; and ability to meet deadlines

· Physical: Computer keyboarding, travel as required

· Auditory/Visual: Hearing, vision and talking

They are not intended to constitute a comprehensive list of functions, duties, or local variances. Management retains the discretion to add or to change the duties of the position at any time.

jobs.title: Cognitief gedragstherapeutisch werker (CGW) – GGz Online
jobs.excerpt: Jouw vak, volledig online Als cognitief gedragstherapeutisch werker (CGW) begeleid je volwassenen vanaf 18 jaar met onder andere angststoornissen, depressieve klachten en trauma- en stressgerelateerde problematiek.
jobs.description:
Jouw vak, volledig online

Als cognitief gedragstherapeutisch werker (CGW) begeleid je volwassenen vanaf 18 jaar met onder andere angststoornissen, depressieve klachten en trauma- en stressgerelateerde problematiek. Je werkt binnen kortdurende, intensieve behandeltrajecten met een gemiddelde duur van drie maanden.

Je helpt cliënten om niet-helpende gedachten en gedragspatronen te herkennen en te veranderen. Daarvoor voer je zelfstandig cognitief-gedragstherapeutische interventies uit, binnen de kaders van het behandelplan en in afstemming met de betrokken behandelaren.

Bij cliënten met angstklachten begeleid je bijvoorbeeld exposure-oefeningen en gedragsexperimenten. Bij depressieve klachten kun je gedragsactivatie inzetten. Je bespreekt de voortgang en helpt cliënten om nieuwe vaardigheden daadwerkelijk toe te passen in hun dagelijks leven. ]Concreet betekent dit dat je:

  • CGT-interventies uitvoert volgens evidence-based behandelprotocollen, zoals exposure, gedragsactivatie en cognitieve technieken.

  • cliënten begeleidt bij oefeningen, huiswerkopdrachten en gedragsexperimenten.

  • samen met cliënten onderzoekt welke gedachten en gedragspatronen hun klachten in stand houden.

  • de voortgang volgt, resultaten evalueert en bevindingen bespreekt met betrokken behandelaren.

  • beeldbellen, online behandelmodules en passende digitale toepassingen inzet.

  • deelneemt aan multidisciplinaire overleggen en bijdraagt aan de ontwikkeling van digitaal behandelen.

Volledig online behandelen vraagt dat je ook op afstand goed kunt aansluiten bij cliënten. Je biedt structuur en helpt hen actief met hun behandeling aan de slag te gaan.

Zelfstandig betekent niet alleen

Je voert zelfstandig CGT-interventies uit, maar staat er inhoudelijk niet alleen voor. Je werkt binnen de kaders van het behandelplan en maakt deel uit van een multidisciplinair team met onder anderen psychologen, verpleegkundigen, ervaringsdeskundigen en psychiaters.

Je stemt met de betrokken behandelaar af over behandeldoelen en interventies. Tijdens de behandeling volg je hoe cliënten reageren op oefeningen en welke vooruitgang zij boeken. Wanneer een interventie onvoldoende resultaat oplevert of de problematiek complexer blijkt, bespreek je dit met de behandelaar.

Zo combineer je zelfstandig werken binnen je eigen deskundigheid met de inhoudelijke samenwerking die nodig is voor goede zorg.

Zo ziet werken bij GGz Online eruit

GGz Online is de digitale poli van GGz Centraal en biedt specialistische geestelijke gezondheidszorg volledig online. Niet alleen het contact met cliënten is digitaal; ook de manier van samenwerken en behandelen is daarop ingericht.

Je werkt vanuit een professionele thuiswerkplek en organiseert een groot deel van je werkdag zelfstandig. Behandelgesprekken voer je via beeldbellen. Daarnaast maak je gebruik van online behandelmodules waarmee cliënten ook tussen gesprekken door aan hun behandeling kunnen werken.

Je bespreekt bijvoorbeeld hoe een exposure-oefening is verlopen, helpt een cliënt bij het herkennen van automatische gedachten of evalueert de stappen bij het doorbreken van vermijdingsgedrag.

GGz Online biedt op werkdagen behandelingen tussen 08.00 en 20.00 uur. Wanneer je in de avond behandelt, stem je je werktijden daarop af.

Past deze manier van werken bij jou?

Volledig online behandelen vraagt zelfstandigheid en het vermogen om ook digitaal een professionele behandelrelatie op te bouwen. Je hebt niet voortdurend collega's fysiek om je heen en organiseert je werk voor een belangrijk deel zelf.

Je past bij deze manier van werken als je:

  • zelfstandig en zorgvuldig CGT-interventies kunt uitvoeren.

  • cliënten kunt motiveren om gedragspatronen te veranderen.

  • gestructureerd werkt en de behandelvoortgang goed kunt volgen.

  • digitaal vaardig bent en openstaat voor online behandeltechnieken.

  • verantwoordelijkheid neemt en tijdig afstemming zoekt met collega's.

Requirements

Dit heb je nodig

Voor deze functie heb je:

  • een passende afgeronde hbo-opleiding, zoals Social Work (uitstroomprofiel Zorg), SPH, MWD of hbo-Verpleegkunde;

  • een VGCt-registratie als cognitief gedragstherapeutisch werker of een afgeronde, erkende post-hbo-opleiding tot cognitief gedragstherapeutisch werker;

  • ruime ervaring met het uitvoeren van CGT-interventies en kennis van behandelprotocollen.

Daarnaast ben je bij voorkeur minimaal één avond per week beschikbaar om tot 20.00 uur te behandelen.

Wat je van ons krijgt

Als cognitief gedragstherapeutisch werker bij GGz Online krijg je de ruimte om jouw vak zelfstandig uit te oefenen, samen te werken met verschillende disciplines en ervaring op te doen met volledig digitaal behandelen.

Daarnaast kun je rekenen op:

  • een bruto maandsalaris volgens CAO GGZ, FWG 50 (€ 3.456,- tot € 4.579,- op basis van 36 uur). Bereken hier jouw netto salaris.

  • een vast contract voor 24 tot 32 uur per week, met een beoogde startdatum vanaf 1 maart 2027;

  • 8,33% vakantietoeslag en 8,33% eindejaarsuitkering.

  • 166 verlofuren en 35 levensfase-uren op basis van 36 uur.

  • een jaarlijks balansbudget van € 1.000,- naar rato, te besteden aan bijvoorbeeld een opleiding, extra salaris of verlofuren.

  • een thuiswerkbudget van € 450,- voor het inrichten van je werkplek.

  • de mogelijkheid om via de WKR fiscaalvriendelijk een (elektrische) fiets of extra vakantiedagen te kopen.

Ook bieden we ruimte om je vakinhoudelijk te ontwikkelen via opleidingen, trainingen, interne scholing en verbeterinitiatieven.

Onze arbeidsvoorwaarden zijn conform de CAO GGZ.

Klaar om te solliciteren?

Past deze manier van behandelen bij jou en voldoe je aan de functie-eisen? Solliciteer dan via de sollicitatieknop. Zodra we een passende kandidaat hebben gevonden, kunnen we de vacature eerder sluiten.

Eerst weten hoe dit in de praktijk werkt?

Benieuwd hoe je als cognitief gedragstherapeutisch werker volledig online behandelt? Of wil je meer weten over de CGT-interventies, de samenwerking met behandelaren of de inrichting van je werkdag? Neem dan contact op met Carlos Croes, klinisch psycholoog/manager zorg, via +31 6 53479468.

Een referentiecheck maakt onderdeel uit van het aannamebeleid. Bij indiensttreding vragen we een actuele Verklaring Omtrent Gedrag (VOG) aan en vergoeden we de kosten.

Highlights

Je begeleidt volwassenen met psychische klachten met cognitief-gedragstherapeutische interventies. Volledig online, zelfstandig binnen het behandelplan en in afstemming met andere behandelaren.

jobs.excerpt: At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?
jobs.description:
At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it.

Location: Remote - United Kingdom

Education: PhD or MSc in Health Economics or related field

Experience: 10+ years in HEOR

Travel: Required for congresses and key engagements

What if your models could get life-changing medicines to patients faster?

At Bristol Myers Squibb, we believe that the best science deserves the best chance of reaching the people who need it most. That's where you come in.

As an Associate Director within our Global Health Economics and Outcomes Research (GHEOR) Evidence Acceleration & Innovation (EAI) team, you won't just be building models - you'll be shaping the evidence that determines whether patients across the world can access transformative therapies. Your work will sit at the intersection of cutting-edge AI, rigorous health economics, and real-world impact.

This is a role for someone who is technically exceptional, intellectually curious, and motivated by knowing that the analysis they run today could change a patient's access to treatment tomorrow.

What You'll Be Doing

You'll be a scientific voice within a team that pushes the boundaries of what health economics can achieve. Day to day, this means:

  • Driving innovation in HTA methodology - not following best practice but helping to define it. You'll horizon-scan advances from academia, payers, and competitors, and embed those learnings into how BMS approaches value demonstration globally.
  • Putting AI to work - you'll lead and execute automation workstreams and deliver market-level cost-effectiveness model adaptations using BMS's own MAx Generative AI tool suite. This is a genuine opportunity to be on the frontier of AI-driven HEOR at a top-tier global biopharma.
  • Shaping pipeline decisions - you'll build early economic models that directly inform whether promising assets move forward. Your analytical judgement will have a seat at the table where it counts.
  • Influencing payer and HTA strategy - you'll contribute to BMS's external strategy to evolve how payer and HTA agencies assess the value of our portfolio, engaging directly with reimbursement authorities and contributing to submissions worldwide.
  • Being a trusted collaborator - working across global, regional, and local teams, partnering with GHEOR asset leads, affiliates and external contractors, and serving as an active member of the Model Protocol Review Committee.
  • Delivering hands-on - whether it's structural updates to economic models, indirect treatment comparisons, or providing HEOR analytics to inform pricing strategy, you'll be someone who can lead and do.

What This Role Gives You

  • Genuine influence - you'll shape the methodologies that determine market access for BMS's portfolio, not just execute them
  • A platform to innovate - with BMS's investment in Generative AI and the MAx tool suite, you'll be working with tools and approaches that most HEOR professionals are only reading about
  • Global reach - your work will span markets worldwide, giving you exposure to payer environments and regulatory landscapes across Europe and beyond
  • Scientific credibility - active participation in external strategy, congresses, and published research means your professional profile grows alongside your impact
  • Flexibility - this role is fully remote in the UK, trusting you to deliver in the way that works best for you

What We're Looking For

You'll bring a strong technical foundation paired with the strategic mindset to lead. Specifically, we're looking for:

Qualifications & Experience

  • A PhDorMSc in Health Economics or a closely related discipline
  • 10+ years of HEOR experience, with a strong track record in model development and HTA submissions
  • Experience working with payers and HTA authorities across multiple markets
  • Published research in health economic modelling or innovative HTA methodology - your name on the work matters to us
  • A working understanding of Generative AI techniques and their application in automating HEOR workflows, with an awareness of the risks (biases, inaccuracies) that need to be managed

Technical Skills

Essential

  • Excel (Advanced)
  • R and/or Python
  • Visual Basic (VBA)

Desirable

  • OpenBUGS / WinBUGS
  • JAGS

You should be comfortable not just using these tools but reading, interpreting and modifying existing code - rolling up your sleeves when the model needs hands-on attention.


Beyond the Technical

  • Strong project management skills - you can lead complex, multi-stakeholder workstreams and keep them on track
  • Excellent communication skills - able to translate complex economic evidence for diverse audiences, from internal matrix partners to HTA authorities
  • A collaborative instinct - you thrive in a broad matrix environment and bring others along with you

A Note on Travel

You'll have the opportunity to represent BMS at key congresses and attend internal and external engagements throughout the year. For someone who values staying connected to the broader scientific community, this is a genuine perk.


We hire for skills and capabilities, not just credentials – if this role excites you, but doesn’t perfectly match your resume, we encourage you to apply anyway.


How We Work

Where you work matters – because collaboration, innovation and patient impact happen in many settings. Our roles are structured across four work models: site-essential, site-by-design, field-based and remote-by-design. The model assigned to this role is based on its core responsibilities. jobs.description:
Marcus Evans is a global leader in business intelligence, helping our clients grow by making connections, sharing knowledge, inspiring people, building relationships and creating new opportunities. With over four decades of experience and teams of highly experienced professionals across 50+ office locations, we deliver impactful strategic insight and business development guidance across all sectors through high-level summits, conferences, online platforms, performance coaching, and curated corporate event programmes. Based in 30+ countries, we create services that connect decision-makers, spark innovation, and drive real business growth.

ME Perform is the performance improvement consultancy of the Marcus Evans Group. We work differently from most of the training market: we diagnose what is actually holding an organisation's people back, design a programme specifically for them, deliver it over months rather than days, and measure whether behaviour genuinely changed, then hand the client written evidence of what improved. Because the design work is done in-house by our Programme Scientists, our trainers get something rare: a fully built, properly researched session, briefed to them in advance, delivered to a cohort who have already been diagnosed and who are expecting to work rather than watch.

Job Summary

You will deliver live sessions, typically 90 to 150 minutes, mostly online, working from a session design and a written brief prepared for you by the Programme Scientist.

This is a delivery role, and deliberately so. You are not asked to write content, find clients, or sell anything. You are asked to be outstanding in the room. Based on the seniority and ability of the applicant there will also be an opportunity extend this role to a follow-up coach with the same group.

Key Responsibilities

  • Deliver live sessions to our designed structure, to a consistently high standard.

  • Prepare from the written brief you receive at least five working days before each session — preparation time is paid within the session fee.

  • Run structured practice: our sessions are built around participants doing the thing, not listening to it explained. Expect to spend much of each session facilitating small-group work, giving feedback, and coaching in the moment.

  • Manage the room — including the sceptical senior participant, the quiet group, and the one who wants to debate rather than practise.

  • Submit brief written session notes within 48 hours of every session, so the Programme Scientist can adjust what comes next.

  • Take part in accreditation before your first client session, and stay open to observation and feedback afterwards.

Qualifications

Essential

  • 5-10 years of substantial experience in facilitating live learning or development sessions for professional or managerial audiences in a corporate setting.

  • Genuinely strong online delivery — confident running breakout groups, keeping cameras on and energy up, and handling the mechanics without it disrupting the session.

  • Comfortable delivering material you did not write, to a structure you are asked to keep to. This is the single most important requirement of the role.

  • Skilled at running practice and giving direct, useful feedback to adults — rather than presenting.

  • Reliable on the administrative side: punctual, responsive, and consistent with session notes.

  • Fluent, credible professional English, and comfortable with senior audiences.

Desirable

  • Experience in one or more of: leadership and management development, communication and influence, collaboration, resilience and change, or working across cultures.

  • A coaching qualification, or experience delivering one-to-one as well as group work.

  • Additional languages, or experience delivering to international cohorts working in a second language.

  • Familiarity with evidence-based learning design — you do not need to be a researcher, but you should be interested in why a session is built the way it is.

How the engagement works

  • Paid accreditation first: a methodology induction, then you deliver a full session for our Programme Scientist to observe, paid at half the standard session fee. Accreditation is completed before any client-facing work.

  • You are then briefed and booked per session. Fees are paid per session with preparation included, invoiced on delivery, on 30-day terms.

  • Standard contract terms apply, including confidentiality, intellectual property assignment for anything created in connection with the work, and non-solicitation of our clients. These are shared in full before accreditation.

  • If a client cancels at short notice, you are protected: cancellations inside five working days are paid in full.

Marcus Evans is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment where all employment decisions are based on qualifications, merit, and business need.

Job Title: Member of Legal Staff, Legal AI Product Lead

Job Type: Full-time

Location: Remote- US Only

About the role

We’re looking for an AI-native lawyer who loves solving legal problems and building things. At micro1, we’re rethinking how a legal function should operate in the AI era. We believe a small team of exceptional lawyers, supported by powerful AI agents and purpose-built technology, can operate at a scale and speed that traditional legal departments cannot.

You’ll work directly with our General Counsel, legal team, and engineering team to identify legal problems, design and build AI-powered solutions, and continuously improve how legal work gets done.

Your initial focus will be developing AI agents and automating high-value legal workflows. Over time, you’ll help bring these capabilities together into a fully integrated, proprietary legal platform — the central hub for legal work at micro1.

This is a hands-on building role. You don’t need to be a software engineer, but you do need to love building, experimenting, and turning ideas into working solutions. We’re looking for a natural problem solver who combines strong legal reasoning with technical curiosity, creativity, and exceptional execution.

What you’ll do

  1. Solve legal problems with technology. Identify inefficiencies, bottlenecks, and recurring challenges across the legal function, and develop creative, practical solutions using AI.
  2. Build AI-powered legal agents and workflows. Personally prototype solutions using AI and no-code/low-code tools, and partner closely with our engineering team to develop and deploy more sophisticated systems.
  3. Own the product development process. Translate legal problems into product requirements, prioritize features, work directly with engineers, and drive solutions from concept through deployment.
  4. Evaluate and improve AI agents. Partner with our legal and operations teams to develop rigorous evaluations, test cases, and quality standards that reflect our legal team’s judgment, preferences, and risk tolerance. Continuously iterate until solutions meet those standards.
  5. Build our internal legal platform. Help design and develop an integrated, AI-native platform that connects legal intake, contracting, approvals, knowledge management, and other legal workflows.
  6. Practice law. Own basic substantive legal work, particularly commercial contracting, while developing deeper legal expertise alongside senior members of our team.

Who we’re looking for

  1. JD from a leading U.S. law school, ideally with 0–5 years of post-graduation experience.
  2. Demonstrated experience building something with AI. This is essential. Whether it’s an agent, application, automation, workflow, or other tool, you must have personally built something meaningful and be able to demonstrate it.
  3. Exceptional problem-solving ability. You instinctively break down complex, ambiguous problems, identify the underlying issues, and find creative ways to solve them.
  4. A genuine builder mentality. You love experimenting, prototyping, testing, and iterating. You’re excited to be personally involved in building solutions, not just managing projects or vendors.
  5. AI fluency and technical curiosity. You’re deeply engaged with emerging AI capabilities and excited to explore what they make possible. Coding experience is a plus, not a requirement.
  6. High agency and ownership. You’re resourceful, move quickly, and thrive in a fast-moving environment with substantial autonomy.We can teach you commercial contracting and other areas of substantive law. What we’re looking for is harder to teach: exceptional intellectual curiosity, legal problem-solving ability, product instincts, and a genuine passion for building.

Why this role is different

  1. This isn’t a traditional attorney position, a legal operations role, or a conventional product management job.
  2. You’ll combine substantive legal work with the opportunity to personally build the technology that transforms how our legal department operates. You’ll have direct exposure to the General Counsel, dedicated engineering support, and meaningful ownership over the solutions we develop.
  3. We’re looking for someone who doesn’t just want to practice law more efficiently. We want someone who wants to reinvent how legal work gets done.

How to apply

Show us something you’ve built with AI.

As part of the application process, we’ll ask you to demonstrate a tool, agent, application, automation, or workflow that you’ve personally built.

It doesn’t need to involve writing code or be a polished, production-ready product. We want to understand the problem you identified, how you approached solving it, what you personally built, and how you evaluated whether it worked.

We’re much more interested in your creativity, problem-solving ability, and enthusiasm for building than the sophistication of the underlying technology.

All employees are eligible for equity compensation, and employees may also receive performance-based bonuses, dependent on role and subject to company policies. micro1 provides a comprehensive benefits package, including up to 100% reimbursement for health-insurance premiums, paid time off, a 401(K) plan with a company match, and additional benefits designed to support a high-performing, remote-first workforce.

dein profil - das bringst du mit:

warum wir?

  • Homeoffice & Flexibilität: Du arbeitest deutschlandweit aus dem Homeoffice und profitierst von einem hohen Maß an Eigenverantwortung.

Die Position ist in Vollzeit mit 40 Stunden pro Woche zu besetzen. Teilzeit ist nicht möglich. Arbeitsbeginn ist üblicherweise zwischen 7:00 und 8:30 Uhr, in Abstimmung mit deinem Vorgesetzten und dem Team.

This is a US-based remote role. You will be required to interview in person.


About SailPoint:

SailPoint is defining the next era of identity security. Our unified, AI-powered platform seamlessly secures both the Human Fabric of your workforce and the Agentic Fabric of AI and non-human identities, completely eliminating organizational blind spots.


Built on core principles like zero-standing privilege and contextualized risk, our platform transforms identity from a vulnerability into a strategic business advantage. Today, we are trusted by some of the largest, most complex organizations in the world to deliver intelligent, autonomous identity security at scale.


About the Role:

As the Principal Product Manager for Government, Geography, and Compliance (GGC), you will lead product strategy and define the envelope for how SailPoint extends identity security to customers in heavily regulated industries, public-sector environments, and sovereign global markets.


In this role, you will own market choices, product vision, requirements, prioritization, scope, success criteria, and the business cases and budgets that fund delivery across parallel programs. You will build a deep understanding of these markets, tracking where regulation and customer demand are heading, and develop direct relationships with key customers and our Sales teams. You will serve as the single product authority, translating complex compliance and regional mandates into high-impact, cloud-native capabilities while collaborating across Engineering, Operations, Program Management, Security, IT, Compliance, FP&A, Legal, and Go-To-Market (GTM) teams.


Roadmap for Success:


Please note: Key initiatives within this portfolio are already in progress. Specific milestones and timelines outlined below are subject to adjustment based on ongoing progress and business needs.


30 days:

  • Complete onboarding, gain familiarity with SailPoint’s Identity Security Cloud Platform architecture, and review the current portfolio of GGC initiatives across government, geography, and compliance.
  • Establish working relationships with key cross-functional partners in Program Management, Engineering, Operations, Compliance, Security, IT, Legal, Sales, and FP&A.
  • Audit and review active program scopes, certification timelines (e.g., FedRAMP, DoD impact levels, PCI DSS, ISO), and regional deployment milestones.

60 days:

  • Assume ownership of the single prioritized GGC product roadmap, reconciling parallel program streams and identifying immediate interdependencies including communication of the roadmap cross-functionally.
  • Conduct baseline control-gap and option analyses across active sovereign and in-country infrastructure initiatives to evaluate scope vs. delivery commitments.
  • Partner with FP&A and cross-functional budget owners to review and update existing business cases, revenue/cost models, and program budgets.

90 days:

  • Formulate and publish the comprehensive GGC product strategy and vision, defining clear prioritization frameworks for pursuing, pausing, or retiring specific compliance and regional programs.
  • Finalize detailed Product Requirement Documents (PRDs), scope definitions, and success metrics for upcoming quarterly delivery cycles.
  • Align with Engineering leadership on backlog prioritization and with Program Management on integrated critical paths and dependency tracking.

6 months:

  • Successfully drive product readiness and scope validation for targeted GGC certification milestones and sovereign market rollouts.
  • Establish field-ready narratives, customer commitment timelines, and go-to-market enablement collateral in collaboration with Sales and GTM teams.
  • Conduct formal quarterly business reviews of the GGC investment portfolio, presenting executive-level go/no-go recommendations and financial models.

1 year:

  • Deliver measurable expansion in SailPoint’s addressable regulated and sovereign markets by achieving planned government authorizations and geographic deployment milestones.
  • Institutionalize repeatable frameworks for scoping, building, and launching emerging compliance frameworks (e.g., AI governance and local data residency standards).
  • Serve as the recognized organizational authority and external evangelist for SailPoint's GGC product direction with customers, analysts, and strategic cloud partners.

Requirements:


  • BA/BS in business or technical field required. MBA is a plus.
  • 10+ years of product management experience, including 3+ years focused on regulated cloud SaaS, public sector offerings, data sovereignty/residency, or multi-program compliance portfolios
  • Proven depth across GGC domains: government authorization models (e.g., FedRAMP, DoD IL), regional deployment/data residency models, and enterprise compliance attestations
  • Demonstrated track record of owning product vision, PRDs, scope definitions, and prioritized roadmaps across multiple parallel programs, including dependency management
  • Strong financial acumen and experience building business cases, revenue/cost models, and portfolio budget analyses
  • Proven cross-functional leadership and executive communication skills with Engineering, Program Management, Legal, Security, and Sales teams
  • Ability to travel approximately 15%

Preferred Skills:


  • Master of Business Administration (MBA) or advanced degree in a technical field
  • Domain background in Identity and Access Management (IAM) or cybersecurity products
  • Direct experience with high-assurance, sovereign, air-gapped, or critical-infrastructure environments
  • Professional credentials such as CISSP, CIPP, PMP, or equivalent certifications

Benefits:

At SailPoint, our identity security innovations are powered by a global crew. We are proudly headquartered in Austin, Texas, with a beautiful campus that overlooks the scenic 4 Points Preserve. We embrace a flexible, remote-first work culture that prioritizes personal autonomy, trust, and work-life balance. We provide:

WORK OPTION: Remote

Position Summary

The National Basketball Association (NBA) is seeking a hands-on Staff Engineer, AI Engineering Practices to own AI practices across Software Engineering and Program Delivery. Reporting to the Vice President, Software Engineering & Program Delivery, this role is the single owner accountable for AI engineering standards, tool governance and the AI-native product development lifecycle (AI-DLC), and for scaling AI-enabled practices across engineering teams and technical program managers (TPMs).


AI transformation is an organizational priority area, but today it relies on leaders who already run people and project delivery, which limits how fast the organization can transform. Adoption is fragmented across teams and dependent on individual leaders. The Staff Engineer will change that by building practices that are repeatable, governed and measured: tool-agnostic standards for agentic coding and spec-driven development, reusable agentic pipelines and context engineering frameworks, and structured evaluations of new tools.


This is a practitioner role. The Director builds hands-on, works credibly with both engineers and program managers, and brings the same AI capability to TPMs for planning, forecasting, status reporting and risk management. Early priorities are standard AI engineering frameworks for GitHub Copilot, Claude Code and Atlassian Rovo, and an AI-DLC engineering workflow.

Major Responsibilities


AI Engineering Standards and Tool Governance


  • Own AI engineering standards and tool governance across Software Engineering and Program Delivery, replacing fragmented, leader-dependent adoption with one accountable approach.
  • Set tool-agnostic standards for agentic coding and spec-driven development.
  • Deliver standard AI engineering frameworks for GitHub Copilot, Claude Code and Atlassian Rovo as a first priority.
  • Keep the development lifecycle tool-agnostic across Claude Code, GitHub Copilot and Codex, so that practices do not depend on any single tool.

AI-Native Development Lifecycle (AI-DLC)


  • Own the AI-native PDLC / AI-DLC for Software Engineering and Program Delivery.
  • Design and roll out an AI-DLC engineering workflow as a priority roadmap item.
  • Create a repeatable, governed and measurable operating capability behind the workflow, so that it does not depend on individual leaders.

Agentic Pipelines, Frameworks and Automation


  • Build reusable agentic pipelines hands-on, as a practitioner.
  • Build context and harness engineering frameworks that engineering teams can adopt and reuse.
  • Build AI-enabled automations that reduce administrative overhead across engineering and program delivery.

Tool Evaluation and Measurement


  • Run structured evaluations of new AI tools and make the adopt / hold / drop decision.
  • Track and report the share of developers and TPMs actively using AI capabilities.
  • Report AI token cost and headcount cost per project.
  • Measure and report improvement in delivery velocity, software quality and administrative overhead.

Enablement for Engineering Teams and TPMs


  • Enable engineering teams and TPMs on AI adoption, patterns and practice.
  • Bring AI-enabled planning, forecasting, status reporting and risk management to Program Delivery value streams.
  • Serve as the credible bridge between engineers and program managers on how AI changes the way work is planned, built and reported.

Required Education and Professional Experience


  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Background as a senior engineer or engineering leader, with 8 years of relevant experience.
  • Demonstrated hands-on experience running agentic tooling in production.
  • Practical experience with AI engineering tools such as GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Codex and Atlassian Rovo.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities


  • Hands-on practitioner who builds as well as directs: agentic pipelines, context and harness engineering, and AI-enabled automation.
  • Working command of agentic coding and spec-driven development practices.
  • Ability to design structured tool evaluations and make clear adopt / hold / drop decisions.
  • Ability to set standards and governance that are repeatable and measured, without locking the organization into a single tool.
  • Credibility with both engineers and program managers.
  • Ability to translate AI capability into practical planning, forecasting, status reporting and risk management for TPMs.
  • Comfort reporting adoption, cost and delivery outcomes in plain terms, including AI token cost and headcount cost per project.

Salary Range:

$240,000-$260,000

Job Posting Title:

Senior Director

Employees currently are eligible to receive an annual discretionary performance bonus, awarded at the sole discretion of the Company and subject to any terms and conditions set by the Company. Employees and/or eligible dependents may be eligible to participate in the following Company-sponsored employee benefit programs: medical; dental; vision; life/AD&D insurance; short- and long-term disability; fertility and family-forming assistance; wellbeing allowance; educational assistance; mental health coaching/therapy; tax advantaged accounts such as HSA and healthcare/dependent care FSAs; a 401(k) retirement plan; and time off benefits that include vacation, sick time, and personal days.


We Consider Applicants For All Positions On The Basis Of Merit, Qualifications And Business Needs, And Without Regard To Race, Color, National Origin, Religion, Sex, Gender Identity, Age, Disability, Alienage Or Citizenship Status, Ancestry, Marital Status, Creed, Genetic Predisposition Or Carrier Status, Sexual Orientation, Veteran Status, Familial Status, Status As A Victim Of Domestic Violence Or Any Other Status Or Characteristic Protected By Applicable Federal, State, Or Local Law.


About the NBA

The National Basketball Association (NBA) is a global sports and media organization with the mission to inspire and connect people everywhere through the power of basketball. Built around five professional sports leagues: the NBA, WNBA, NBA G League, NBA 2K League and Basketball Africa League, the NBA has established a major international presence with games and programming available in 214 countries and territories in more than 50 languages, and merchandise for sale in more than 200 countries and territories on all seven continents. NBA rosters at the start of the 2026-27 season featured 125 international players from a record-tying 43 countries across six continents. The NBA's digital assets include NBA TV, NBA.com, the NBA App and NBA League Pass. The NBA has created one of the largest social media communities in the world, with more than 2.5 billion likes and followers globally across all leagues, team and player platforms. The NBA's Tap to Watch provides seamless access to local, national and global live game telecasts via the NBA App, NBA.com, third-party digital platforms and NBA partner platforms. NBA Cares, the NBA's global social impact platform, drives change on issues facing fans and communities in the areas of health and wellness, civic engagement, social justice and inclusion, and sustainability.

We are looking for a Field Marketing Manager based in Brazil to build the pipeline engine that powers DEUNA's regional sales team.   • Define the event strategy: which events to attend, goals, target account invitations, pre-event outreach, on-site execution, and post-event follow-up with Sales.

PR & Communications

  • Build and execute the PR strategy for Brazil and the region: press releases, media relations, executive thought leadership, awards, and analyst/industry visibility.

  • Adapt and create content in Portuguese, Spanish, and English: website, case studies, decks, one-pagers, social, and sales enablement materials.

  • Strong project management, analytical, and communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Knowledge of the Brazilian payments and e-commerce ecosystem (PIX, installments, local acquirers, marketplaces).

Success Metrics

  • Marketing-sourced and SDR-sourced qualified pipeline in Brazil.

  • Earned media coverage and share of voice in target outlets.

Das bringst du mit

jobs.excerpt: Job Description: DXC Technology is a global technology services company, helping organisations modernise their IT, transform their operations and make the most of technology to deliver better business outcomes.
jobs.description:
Job Description:

DXC Technology is a global technology services company, helping organisations modernise their IT, transform their operations and make the most of technology to deliver better business outcomes.

Within our Insurance Software business, we work with insurance organisations to support some of their most important business processes through specialist software, technology and services. Our teams combine deep insurance knowledge with technology expertise, working closely with clients to build long-term relationships and help them respond to an evolving insurance market.

Joining our Insurance Software team means becoming part of a collaborative business where commercial, technology, delivery and client teams work together to deliver successful outcomes for our customers.

The Opportunity

We’re looking for an experienced Commercial Contracts Manager to join our Insurance Software business and support the effective commercial and contractual management of our client relationships.

Working as part of the wider account team, you’ll be involved throughout the contract lifecycle, from initiation and negotiation through to execution, change and ongoing management. You’ll help ensure contractual commitments are clearly understood, changes are managed effectively, potential risks are identified early and positive commercial outcomes are achieved.

This is a practical, hands-on role for someone with solid commercial contract management experience who enjoys working collaboratively with account, delivery and client teams. You’ll develop a strong understanding of our client contracts while playing an important role in protecting DXC’s contractual position and supporting successful client relationships.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Provide day-to-day commercial contract support across our Insurance Software client portfolio.
  • Manage and support contracts throughout their lifecycle, including initiation, negotiation, execution, amendments, renewals, variations, change control and ongoing contract management.
  • Review and interpret contractual terms and conditions, ensuring obligations, commitments and entitlements are clearly understood and appropriately managed.
  • Support contract negotiations and approvals, working with clients and internal stakeholders to achieve practical and commercially balanced outcomes.
  • Assist with the drafting and review of contractual documentation, agreements and contract changes, using appropriate templates and standard agreements.
  • Identify contractual and commercial risks, highlighting potential issues and supporting appropriate mitigation and resolution.
  • Help ensure contracts are managed in accordance with contractual terms and relevant legal, regulatory and internal requirements.
  • Monitor contractual obligations and commitments, following up with relevant stakeholders where required.
  • Support the resolution of contractual issues and disputes, working collaboratively with account, delivery, finance, legal and other internal teams.
  • Develop a strong understanding of individual client contracts, identifying opportunities to protect DXC’s contractual position and improve commercial outcomes.
  • Support contract governance and commercial reviews, ensuring appropriate documentation and records are maintained.
  • Build effective working relationships with client stakeholders and colleagues across the Insurance Software business.
  • Respond to contract-related queries and provide clear, practical commercial and contractual guidance to account and delivery teams.

What We’re Looking For

  • Good experience within commercial contract management, contracts or a related commercial environment.
  • Practical experience managing or supporting contracts throughout their lifecycle.
  • Experience reviewing, interpreting and working with contractual terms and conditions and contract documentation.
  • Experience supporting contract negotiations, amendments, variations, change controls and approvals.
  • A good understanding of contractual and commercial risk, with the ability to identify potential issues and escalate appropriately.
  • An understanding of contract law and its practical application within a commercial environment.
  • Strong attention to detail and confidence working with complex contractual information.
  • Good written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain contractual and commercial matters clearly.
  • Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple activities, priorities and deadlines.
  • Confidence working collaboratively with stakeholders across account management, delivery, finance, legal and other business functions.
  • A practical, solutions-focused approach with an interest in continuing to develop your commercial and contractual knowledge.

It Would Be Great If You Also Have

  • Experience within insurance, insurance software, technology or IT services.
  • Experience working with long-term client contracts or within a complex service environment.
  • Knowledge of contract governance, commercial controls and change management processes.
  • A relevant degree or equivalent practical commercial experience.
  • A relevant commercial or contract management qualification, such as CCCM or CPCM, would be advantageous but is not essential.

Why Join Us?

This is a great opportunity to develop your commercial contract management experience within DXC’s Insurance Software business, working alongside colleagues across commercial, account management, delivery, finance and legal.

You’ll join a collaborative environment where you can build your knowledge of client contracts, strengthen your commercial expertise and make a visible contribution to the successful management of our client relationships.

We’re looking for someone who brings sound commercial judgement, attention to detail and a positive, practical approach. You don’t need to know everything from day one. What’s important is having a solid grounding in commercial contract management and the ability and enthusiasm to continue developing your knowledge and experience.

At DXC Technology, we believe strong connections and community are key to our success. Our work model prioritizes in-person collaboration while offering flexibility to support wellbeing, productivity, individual work styles, and life circumstances. We’re committed to fostering an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive.

DXC does not make offers of employment via social media networks and DXC never asks for any money or payments from applicants at any point in the recruitment process, nor ask a job seeker to purchase IT or other equipment on our behalf. jobs.description:
Summary:

VIAVI (NASDAQ: VIAV) has a 90+ year history of technical innovations that have evolved to keep pace and address our customer’s most pressing business issues. We make equipment, software, and systems that help to plan, deploy, certify, monitor, and optimize all kinds of networks - like those for mobile phones, service providers, large businesses and data centers. And, we are also at the forefront of optical security – we bend light to develop and deliver optical solutions that provide security to the world’s currencies and safety and performance applications for consumer electronics and spectrometry.

We are the people behind the products that help keep the world connected – at home, school, work, at play, and everywhere in between. VIAVI employees are fierce about supporting customer success and we welcome people who bring their best every day to the company - to question, to collaborate and to push for solutions that will delight our customers.

Duties & Responsibilities:

Viavi Solutions Inc. is seeking a Global Commodity Director specializing in FPGA components to strategically source, negotiate, and manage supplier relationships for these critical technologies. This role will ensure the availability of high-quality, cost-effective FPGAs to support Viavi's product development and manufacturing needs.

Job Responsibilities:


  • Develop and execute global commodity strategies for FPGA components, aligning with Viavi's overall business objectives and technology roadmaps.
  • Identify, evaluate, and qualify new suppliers for FPGA technologies, conducting thorough due diligence and risk assessments.
  • Negotiate complex agreements with suppliers, including pricing, terms and conditions, intellectual property, and service level agreements, to achieve optimal cost, quality, and delivery.
  • Manage supplier relationships, monitoring performance against key metrics (cost, quality, delivery, innovation, sustainability) and driving continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Collaborate closely with R&D, Engineering, Product Management, and Manufacturing teams to understand current and future FPGA requirements and influence design for manufacturability and cost.
  • Monitor market trends, technological advancements, and supply chain dynamics within the FPGA industry to identify opportunities and mitigate risks.
  • Develop and implement strategies for supply chain continuity and risk management, including identifying alternative sources and developing buffer stock plans.
  • Drive cost reduction initiatives through negotiation, value engineering, and demand aggregation across Viavi's global operations.
  • Ensure compliance with all relevant company policies, ethical standards, and regulatory requirements in procurement activities.
  • Prepare and present reports on commodity performance, market intelligence, and strategic initiatives to senior management.

Pre-Requisites / Skills / Experience Requirements:

Job Qualifications:

jobs.description:
Sales Development Representative (SDR)

100% Remote | Outbound | SaaS | Proptech | Real Estate | Global: Australia, New Zealand, & the USA

Who We Are

AI is the new front door. Renowned makes sure real estate agents are on the other side of it.

We specialise in AI discoverability, ensuring agent data is structured, credible, and consistent so the trust they've built translates into every AI conversation that matters.

We started in 2014 as RateMyAgent, one of the most trusted real estate review platforms in Australia, New Zealand, and the US (ASX: RMY). Following the acquisition of Curated Social in late 2024, we evolved into Renowned - a fully integrated marketing platform built specifically for real estate professionals.

We are a globally distributed team of 60+ across Australia, New Zealand, USA, and the Philippines.

The Role

Renowned is looking for an outbound-first Sales Development Representative (SDR) who thrives on the phone and knows how to build pipeline from the ground up.

This is a 100% outbound hunting role. Your day will be spent proactively researching, targeting, and cold-calling high-producing real estate brokerages across the US. Your objective is to spark genuine commercial interest in Renowned and generate qualified, high-value sales opportunities for our US sales and leadership team - including our Senior Account Executive and Director of Sales (US).

We measure success by revenue and qualified pipeline, not vanity metrics. Because we are actively evolving our US outbound motion, you will collaborate closely with leadership to test messaging, refine channel strategies, and help turn early wins into a scalable outbound engine.

What You’ll Own

  • Proactively map, target, and engage high-performing real estate brokerages across the US market to generate new outbound pipeline.
  • Make cold calling your primary weapon - initiating conversations with busy real estate leaders, handling pushback smoothly, and uncovering real business needs.
  • Pair persistent phone outreach with tailored emails, LinkedIn engagement, custom video, and social touchpoints to cut through the noise.
  • Dig into a brokerage’s current market footprint, digital presence, and tech stack to craft outreach that feels relevant rather than templated.
  • Assess a prospect’s team structure, current software, pain points, budget potential, and timing to ensure only legitimate opportunities enter the pipeline.
  • Use sound business judgment to identify high-value enterprise accounts that warrant deeper sales investment versus smaller, transactional opportunities.
  • Book discovery meetings for the US sales team based on true commercial fit and deal potential, prioritizing conversion over raw meeting volume.
  • Execute structured, persistent follow-up sequences, knowing when to pivot your angle and when to disqualify and move on.
  • Maintain clean, accurate, and up-to-date records of all outreach, call notes, qualification criteria, and pipeline stages in HubSpot.
  • Track and own your personal conversion metrics - from dial-to-connect ratios through to qualified meetings and closed-won revenue.
  • Act as the eyes and ears on the front line, feeding prospect objections and market trends back to Sales, Marketing, and Product to sharpen our positioning.
  • Document winning talk tracks, email templates, and workflows to help build a repeatable outbound blueprint as our US footprint expands.

Who You Are

You have built pipeline from scratch before and understand the grit it takes to turn cold outreach into real revenue. You are comfortable picking up the phone, writing outbound messages that actually get replies, and steering conversations toward a clear next step. You don’t need a rigid script for every scenario - you know how to read a prospect, pivot on the fly, and keep deals moving forward.

You bring commercial honesty to your pipeline. You don’t waste energy nursing stalled deals or chasing dead ends; you can quickly tell the difference between genuine buying intent and polite brush-offs, and you know how to act on both.

You thrive in high-growth environments where the playbook is still being written. Ambiguity doesn’t slow you down - you make smart calls with incomplete information, raise your hand when you need support, and take complete ownership of your number.

We aren't looking for a first-time junior. We’re looking for a proven outbound hunter with solid experience under their belt - someone who is ready to make a major impact in the US market right now, with the drive.

Non-negotiable

  • Proven success generating pipeline in a SDR, BDR, sales or similar outbound revenue role.
  • Significant experience with outbound calling. Cold calling should have been a meaningful part of your previous role, not an occasional activity.
  • The ability to explain your past performance using real metrics such as call volume, conversations, meetings generated, conversion rates and pipeline created.
  • Strong qualification skills. You know how to determine whether an opportunity is worth moving forward rather than simply booking a meeting.
  • Coachability - ability to receive feedback from team and implement
  • Commercial judgment. You understand that not every prospect deserves the same level of sales investment and can prioritize higher-value opportunities.
  • The ability to prospect across different customer segments and adjust your approach based on the size and complexity of the opportunity.
  • Clear, confident, and engaging communication by phone, email and video.
  • Strong organization and CRM discipline.
  • Comfort being measured against visible weekly and monthly performance goals.
  • The ability to work independently in a remote environment.
  • Comfort using modern AI tools for research, personalization, preparation and workflow efficiency.
  • Thrive in a remote setup (this is a 100% work from home role).
  • Must be based in the US with full, unlimited working rights.
  • Ability to accommodate occasional after-hours work to cross-over with the Australian and New Zealand team.

What’s On Offer

  • We are not tied to a particular US-state! We offer 100% remote flexibility - work from anywhere in the US.
  • Direct mentorship and collaboration with our VP of Revenue, Head of US.
  • The best of both worlds: the backing and stability of an established, ASX-listed global tech company paired with the speed, autonomy, and upside of an early-stage US start-up.
  • $60K salary (~$90K OTE) (uncapped commissions!!!)
  • 20 days PTO + 10 sick days + 2 dedicated wellness days + paid day off for your birthday + health benefits.

Applicants must thrive in a remote setup (this is a 100% work from home role), must be based in the US with full, unlimited working rights, and have the ability to accommodate occasional after-hours work to cross-over with the Australian and New Zealand team.
