jobs.title: Staff Platform Engineer
jobs.excerpt: NikoHealth is a rapidly growing SaaS company transforming how Durable Medical Equipment (DME) and Home Medical Equipment (HME) providers operate.
jobs.description:
NikoHealth is a rapidly growing SaaS company transforming how Durable Medical Equipment (DME) and Home Medical Equipment (HME) providers operate. Our innovative, all-in-one platform streamlines business operations, empowering providers to work smarter and more efficiently.

About The Role

This is a newly created role, and one of the first two engineering hires NikoHealth will made in the United States. You'll report directly to the CTO and own how our software gets released and run while working closely with other senior engineers.

We operate dozens of .NET services deployed per-customer on Windows Server and IIS in AWS, managed with Terraform and Octopus Deploy. Across hundreds of provider tenants that's thousands of running application instances. Today a change waits for the next release train, and the train then takes weeks to reach the whole fleet, so end-to-end a given feature takes months. Improving our deployment and development experience is the first job. After that there are dozens of areas of platform investment needed to support how fast we're scaling.

What You'll Do

  • Own our CI/CD pipeline end to end, with the authority to change what it deploys and how.
  • Own developer experience. Reproducible builds, a local environment someone can actually stand up, and fast honest feedback on every change. This is half the job, not a side effect of the other half.
  • Get our automated regression suite running in CI. It exists, it's substantial, and it isn't currently executed.
  • Cut release lead time and get the fleet inside a published, committed release window.
  • Make fleet version state answerable by a query instead of by a person, so anyone can see what a customer is running.
  • Design and publish an access model, so provisioning stops routing through one inbox.
  • Start bringing runtimes and dependencies current, beginning with the shared libraries everything else depends on.
  • Document and share what you learn, so infrastructure knowledge stops being concentrated in one place.

What You'll Bring

  • 5+ years in platform, infrastructure, or DevOps engineering.
  • Production Terraform, including state you owned and drift you had to reconcile.
  • Production Windows Server and IIS, application pools included.
  • End-to-end ownership of a CI/CD pipeline in a previous role.
  • AWS at the level this estate uses it: EC2, ALB, VPC, IAM.
  • A track record of replacing a manual process with a measured and automated one, where you can tell us the before and after.
  • Evidence you've made other engineers faster, not just the systems. Build times, local setup, test feedback, whatever it was.
  • Daily working use of AI coding agents such as Cursor or Claude Code, including the harness around them: tests, project instructions, and a loop you can run again.

Nice to have

  • Octopus Deploy, or another deployment orchestrator you owned.
  • Single-tenant or multi-tenant SaaS at meaningful scale.
  • Healthcare, HIPAA, or another regulated environment.

How we work

This is brownfield and we're honest about it. Some of this estate is well-built and some of it grew. We're not asking you to rewrite it, because hundreds of providers bill claims through it every day. We're asking you to make it measurable, make it safe to change, then change it. If you've built a career inheriting other people's systems and making them boring, you'll like it here.

We work with AI agents, seriously. The team works agentically and so will you. What matters is what you do after the agent produces something: tests, linters, project instructions, a loop you can run again. If your answer to a bad result is a longer prompt, we're probably not a fit. This is also why developer experience sits in this role rather than somewhere else: an agent is only as good as the feedback loop it runs in, and ours needs work.

Most application development is done by a long-standing engineering partner. You'd own the pipeline, the infrastructure, and the environments, and over time the standards their code meets before it ships while working closely with our off-shore development team.

Two people isn't a platform team, it's the start of one. Until it's three, coverage is shared between you, the CTO, and our head of engineering. Everyone here is remote, and we'd like your hours to overlap the US East Coast.

This is the start of the engineering team, not the end of it. We're hiring more engineers through 2027. The people who join first get the widest scope, the most say in how the team gets built, and first choice about what they own as it grows.

How to apply

Apply through the link on this page. Instead of a cover letter, we ask one question: tell us about a system you inherited, and the first thing you measured. A few sentences is plenty.

Use AI to help write your application if you want to, we do too. We read every one ourselves, and we can tell when nobody read the posting.

Your first conversation will be with our CTO, who is the hiring manager and will walk you through the rest of the process.

Compensation and benefits

  • The range shown for this role is base salary, and does not include equity or bonus. We post it because we expect to pay inside it.
  • Equity in the company.
  • Medical / dental / vision, 401(k) - up to 4% matching, Unlimited PTO policy

This is a remote role, but candidates must be based in the U.S.

Staff Software Developer (Mobile) - Remote

Intertek, a leading provider of quality and safety solutions to many of the world’s top-recognized brands and companies, is actively seeking a Staff Software Developer (Mobile) to join our People Assurance team as a Remote employee. This is a fantastic opportunity to grow a versatile career in Software Development.

Intertek Alchemy provides frontline worker training solutions for processors, manufacturers, packagers, and distributors of all sizes. Intertek Catalyst inspires and engages workforces with highly creative, custom-branded, asset protection communication programs tailor-made strategic solutions designed to leverage our clients' company brand, values, and objectives to optimize the culture of their people. Intertek is continually innovating and evolving to reduce risk for consumers, brands and organizations in every sector and industry around the world.We go beyond Testing, Inspection and Certification of products: we are a Total Quality Assurance Provider to industries worldwide.Our Purpose: Bringing quality, safety, and sustainability to life.

What are we looking for?

You will own mobile architecture end to end — driving our cross-platform .NET MAUI strategy, setting native implementation standards, and guiding the consolidation of multiple mobile applications onto a single, sustainable codebase. Working across teams, you will set technical direction, raise the engineering bar through design and code review, own the reliability and release health of applications in customers’ hands, and mentor developers at every level. This position outline is a general guideline and does not represent all encompassing details. The position assumes that the incumbent has both the mental and physical requirements to carry out the above defined duties.

jobs.excerpt: At DraftKings, AI is becoming an integral part of both our present and future, powering how work gets done today, guiding smarter decisions, and sparking bold ideas.
jobs.description:
At DraftKings, AI is becoming an integral part of both our present and future, powering how work gets done today, guiding smarter decisions, and sparking bold ideas. It’s transforming how we enhance customer experiences, streamline operations, and unlock new possibilities. Our teams are energized by innovation and readily embrace emerging technology. We’re not waiting for the future to arrive. We’re shaping it, one bold step at a time. To those who see AI as a driver of progress, come build the future together.

The Crown Is Yours

As a Software Architect, you'll help design and scale the systems that power world-class digital experiences. You'll play a critical role in shaping architectural decisions while staying close to the code, ensuring our platforms are resilient, performant, and built to evolve. Working across Engineering, Product, Infrastructure, and Platform teams, you'll influence how we approach distributed systems at scale and elevate technical standards across the organization. Your work will strengthen our foundation today while enabling us to move faster and smarter tomorrow.


DKExchange is DraftKings' regulated prediction markets exchange. In this role you'll take technical ownership of the domain - market data, order entry and matching, request-for-quote trading, clearing and settlement. You'll shape how the platform scales into peak sporting events, how quickly we can add new markets and partners, and how a fast, externally-facing trading system stays correct and available under heavy load.


You'll also work with AI as a core part of how you deliver. We expect our architects to build and own the AI tooling for their domain - agents and automated workflows that handle the repetitive analysis, monitoring and drafting work - so your own time goes to the judgment calls. You'll be hands-on with it, you'll help your teams get good at it, and you'll stay accountable for the quality of what comes out.


What you'll do as a Software Architect


  • Define and evolve architectural solutions that improve system performance, scalability, reliability, and day-to-day operations.
  • Own the technical roadmap for the exchange, and produce the architecture and design for every major initiative in the domain.
  • Maintain the shared foundations - the core patterns, system boundaries, and data contracts that every team builds on, documented clearly enough that both people and AI tools can work from them.
  • Drive consistency in the technologies and patterns used across the exchange's services.
  • Partner closely with Product, Infrastructure, Platform and partner engineering teams - including brokers, market makers and our clearing partners - to build good architectural thinking into planning, design, and delivery.
  • Contribute hands-on to critical work: prototypes, proofs of concept, and production systems that show what scalable, maintainable design looks like.
  • Set and publish the performance and reliability targets for the domain, and lead the load and resilience testing that proves we can meet them before peak events.
  • Guide teams in using proven distributed system patterns, so fault tolerance, observability and operational readiness are built in from day one.
  • Own the operational health of the exchange, using automation and AI tooling to catch problems early and shift from reacting to incidents toward preventing them.
  • Bring architectural expertise to incidents, help drive resolution, and turn what you learn into fixes that stop the same class of failure recurring.
  • Keep an eye on cost, and find and pursue efficiency opportunities as the platform grows.
  • Give thoughtful design reviews and technical guidance that raise the bar across the team, using automated checks for the mechanical issues so review conversations focus on trade-offs.
  • Mentor engineers - on architecture, and on how to work effectively with AI tools in their own day-to-day.
  • Look for where AI can genuinely create leverage in the domain, treat it as a real option alongside traditional approaches, and measure adoption by results: faster delivery, fewer defects, lower cost, new capability.
  • Set sensible guardrails for AI-assisted work - quality checks, boundary validation, and standards that keep things coherent without slowing teams down.
  • Work with engineering leaders to keep architectural decisions aligned with business priorities and long-term platform strategy.

What you'll bring


  • Professional software engineering experience, including significant experience designing and evolving large-scale distributed systems in production.
  • Experience with fast, high-volume transactional or event-driven systems where getting the order and the outcome exactly right matters as much as speed. Background in exchanges, trading, payments or other financial systems is a strong advantage.
  • Extensive knowledge of messaging and streaming systems; hands-on expertise with Kafka is a strong advantage.
  • A solid grasp of how to manage state across a distributed system - how to split and shard data, when to keep it in memory versus a durable store, and the consistency trade-offs involved.
  • Proven understanding of microservices architecture, including containerization and orchestration. Our services are mostly Go and .NET/C#, so comfort working across more than one language stack matters.
  • Familiarity with the protocols and contract-first design this domain runs on - FIX, gRPC and Protobuf - and experience integrating with third-party systems you don't control directly.
  • Working knowledge of relational and NoSQL databases, tradeoffs and advantages based on the use case.
  • Proficiency with modern development practices, including continuous integration and delivery, infrastructure as code, and observability tooling; comfort running load tests and building capacity projections.
  • Real, practical experience using AI tools on production work - coding assistants, agents, automated review and analysis - not just experimentation.
  • A practical view of the economics - able to weigh an AI-based approach against building or buying as part of normal technical decision-making.
  • Exposure to building software in a regulated environment: auditability, data sensitivity, and designing for compliance.
  • Clear, structured communication, with the ability to document decisions and influence both technical and non-technical audiences, including internal and external engineering teams, and other stakeholders.
  • A genuine interest in mentoring engineers, giving useful design feedback, and continuously raising engineering standards.

Join Our Team

We’re a publicly traded (NASDAQ: DKNG) technology company headquartered in Boston. As a regulated gaming company, you may be required to obtain a gaming license issued by the appropriate state agency as a condition of employment. Don’t worry, we’ll guide you through the process if this is relevant to your role.

C++ Software Engineer

Remote (UK-based) | Full-Time

About Us

Reactive Markets is the 2026 OTC Trading Platform of the Year (). Our network handles over $75 billion in daily trading volumes across FX, Equities, and Cryptocurrency, connecting 60+ of the world's leading liquidity providers.

We build trading systems that operate at the edge of what's technically possible — where nanoseconds matter and a dropped message costs real money. Our engineering team is small, senior, and deeply invested in the craft of building cutting edge, reliable, high-performance systems.

The Role

We're looking for a C++ Software Engineer who wants to build low-latency trading infrastructure on Linux. You'll work on the core components of our Switchboard trading platform — pricing engines, connectivity gateways, market-data systems, and the messaging layer that ties them together.

This is not a role where you write code and throw it over a wall. You build it, you test it, you deploy it, you support it in production, and you improve it. Our engineers own the full lifecycle — from design through to operational excellence. When something breaks at 4pm on a Friday, you're part of the team that investigates and fixes it.

Occasional hours outside the normal working day are required for production releases, scheduled maintenance windows, and Level 3 support during critical incidents. We keep this to a minimum and recognise the commitment — but owning a production trading platform means being there when it matters.

What You'll Work On

  • Modern C++20 and Go on Linux — a modern software stack based on open source

  • Cloud-native infrastructure on AWS with colocation in key data centres

  • Microsecond-level latency optimisation and high-throughput messaging

  • Market-data and reference-data pipelines across multiple asset classes

  • FIX protocol integrations with global banks and liquidity providers

  • Observability and monitoring — dashboards, alerting, and metrics that make system behaviour visible

  • Production systems that handle real money — reliability is not optional

What We Need

Technical:

  • Strong C++ with Linux systems programming (3+ years)

  • Comfortable working close to the metal — you understand what's underneath your code

  • Experience with performance-sensitive systems (profiling, optimisation, deterministic behaviour)

  • Familiarity with networking fundamentals (TCP/UDP, socket programming)

  • Go experience is a strong bonus — we use Go extensively for microservices and command-line tooling, and you'll be expected to work with it internally. If you don't know it yet, strong C++ engineers pick it up quickly

  • Python for scripting, automation, testing, and data analysis — used across the platform for tooling and operational workflows

  • Git and shell scripting

  • Experience in financial services or trading technology is a plus but not essential

How you work:

  • You ship. You're delivery-focused — you iterate, you improve, you get things into production

  • You own it. When you build something, you take responsibility for its behaviour in production. You respond to incidents (15-minute acknowledgement SLA during working hours), investigate issues, and close the loop

  • You write things down. Documentation is not an afterthought — it's how we scale knowledge across a distributed team. If it's not written down, it doesn't exist

  • You communicate. We're a distributed team across multiple time zones. Clear, proactive communication — especially when things go wrong — is essential

  • You care about quality. You write clean, testable code. You review your peers' work thoughtfully. You push for continuous improvement without gold-plating

  • You embrace AI tooling. We use AI tools (Claude, Gemini) to amplify our engineering capability — from code review and debugging to incident investigation and documentation. You don't need to be an expert, but you should be curious and willing to learn

What You Get

  • Real problems —trading systems where performance is measured in microseconds, not user clicks

  • An excellent team — senior engineers who care about craft, collaborate openly, and hold each other to high standards

  • Ownership — small teams, clear accountability, direct impact on the platform and our clients

  • Competitive package — up to 30 days leave + bank holidays, private health insurance, pension, life insurance, dental/optical cashback, cycle to work, socials and offsites

  • Remote-friendly — work from home with flexibility. We trust our people to deliver

  • Sustainable pace — we work hard, but we don't burn people out. Balance is how we stay sharp

  • Growth — career progression to senior roles, performance specialisation, or technical leadership. We invest in people who invest in us

We believe in transparency, honest feedback, and writing things down. We celebrate delivery, not activity. We frame AI as empowering people — removing toil, amplifying capability, enabling higher-value work.

We aim to build systems that don't depend on the heroics of individuals to maintain and support — systems and processes that are resilient, documented, and sustainable.

Our Hiring Process

We keep our process focused and respectful of your time. Our process follows three stages.

Stage 1: Initial Conversation with Talent Acquisition

Format: Video call, ~30-45 minutes

Stage 2: Hiring Manager Conversation with the relevant team lead or hiring manager

Format: Video call, ~60 minutes

Stage 3: Technical Interview with two members of the relevant engineering team
Format: Video call, interactive session, ~60 minutes

What to expect in each stage will be explained by Talent Acquisition if you're invited to interview. Throughout the process, we aim to keep momentum with no unnecessary delays between stages, and feedback typically comes within a few business days.

*Please note that depending on availability, Stage 2 and 3 may swap around.

How to Apply

Please apply directly via this job posting — all applications, including those submitted via LinkedIn, are managed through our applicant tracking system, so you'll always land in the same place regardless of where you found this role.

Right to Work: Candidates must have the existing right to work in the UK. We are not currently able to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

Equal Opportunities: Reactive Markets is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage or civil partnership, pregnancy or maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, or sexual orientation.

Reasonable Adjustments: If you need any adjustments or support during the application or interview process, please let us know — we're happy to accommodate.

Data Protection: By applying, you consent to Reactive Markets processing your personal data for recruitment purposes, in line with our privacy policy.

jobs.title: Principal Mini Program Architect OleOle | Platform Architecture & Engineering
jobs.excerpt: We’re not looking for beginners if you don’t have the skill set please do not send your résumé As Principal Mini Program Architect, you will own the technical architecture and engineering direction of OleOle’s Mini Program platform.
jobs.description:
We’re not looking for beginners if you don’t have the skill set please do not send your résumé

As Principal Mini Program Architect, you will own the technical architecture and engineering direction of OleOle’s Mini Program platform.

You will design the infrastructure, developer frameworks, APIs, security architecture, and runtime environment that allow third-party Mini Programs to be created, deployed, discovered, and operated securely at global scale.

This is a hands-on architecture and engineering position, not simply a management role.

You will work closely with OleOle’s frontend, backend, identity, payments, security, and infrastructure engineers to establish a unified technical architecture.

Key Responsibilities

  • Architect the Mini Program runtime, including sandboxed execution, resource management, application lifecycle, and secure integration with the OleOle host platform.
  • Design the Mini Program SDK, APIs, developer tooling, and application frameworks.
  • Establish developer workflows for application creation, testing, submission, review, publishing, deployment, versioning, and updates.
  • Design secure authentication, authorization, identity, and permissions between Mini Programs and the OleOle platform.
  • Integrate Mini Programs with OleOle’s existing identity and Wallet ID architecture, enabling a consistent user identity across applications.
  • Architect integration with OleOle’s payments infrastructure to support transactions, commerce, and financial services within Mini Programs.
  • Define standards for performance, reliability, scalability, isolation, and security.
  • Design application discovery, distribution, and lifecycle management.
  • Establish technical standards, documentation, and development practices for external developers.
  • Make practical architectural decisions that support rapid initial delivery without compromising the platform’s ability to scale.
  • Work directly with engineering teams to implement and validate the architecture.

The successful candidate will have substantial ownership of one of OleOle’s most important long-term technology initiatives.

Skills & Engineering Requirements

Core Technical Expertise

  • 10+ years of professional software engineering experience, with substantial experience designing complex platforms or developer ecosystems.
  • Strong expertise in TypeScript, JavaScript, and modern web application architectures.
  • Deep understanding of browser runtimes, WebViews, JavaScript execution environments, and application sandboxing.
  • Experience designing SDKs, APIs, developer platforms, and extensible application frameworks.
  • Strong knowledge of microservices, distributed systems, backend infrastructure, and event-driven architectures.
  • Experience with secure authentication and authorization, including OAuth 2.0, OIDC, token-based authentication, and permissions management.
  • Knowledge of API security, application isolation, content security policies, and third-party code execution risks.
  • Experience designing high-scale cloud-native systems, preferably using AWS, Kubernetes, Docker, and modern CI/CD pipelines.
  • Strong understanding of application performance, caching, monitoring, observability, and reliability engineering.
  • Ability to translate platform architecture into production-quality engineering implementations.

Highly Valuable Experience

  • Direct experience with WeChat Mini Programs, Alipay Mini Programs, or similar embedded application ecosystems.
  • Experience building developer SDKs, plugin architectures, extensions, application marketplaces, or embedded app frameworks.
  • Familiarity with React, React Native, or comparable frontend frameworks.
  • Experience with mobile-to-web interoperability and cross-platform application delivery.
  • Knowledge of digital wallets, payment orchestration, transaction APIs, and financial platform integration.
  • Experience building developer portals, testing environments, application approval systems, and publishing pipelines.
  • Experience designing platforms that support large numbers of independent third-party developers.

What Matters Most

We are looking for an architect who understands how to build an application ecosystem, not simply an engineer who has developed individual applications.

The ideal candidate combines deep technical expertise, practical engineering judgment, security awareness, and the ability to build foundational technology from the ground up.

Experience with existing Mini Program ecosystems is particularly valuable, but we will also consider outstanding platform architects who have built comparable developer ecosystems, SDKs, application runtimes, or extensible software platforms.

We value engineers who can make decisions, write code, solve difficult architectural problems, and deliver working systems.

Solutions not problems .

  • Creative problem solver who can courageously propose and support new ideas to our organization. Not interested in best practices, lets build something better!
  • Ability to adapt. An ideal candidate will welcome the opportunity to solve a broad range of problems using a wide array of technologies.
  • Comfortable with ambiguity, shifting priorities and general growing pains of an early-stage technology company
  • An exceptional entrepreneurial judgment that fosters independence over micro-management
  • Understanding of football and international sports a huge plus

Deferred compensation

This opportunity is designed for entrepreneurial, startup-minded engineers who want to help build a significant global business. This is not free work. Compensation is agreed upon and deferred until funding is secured, at which point it transitions to a competitive, normalized salary plus equity and OleX token ownership. Our entire team, including the founder, operates under this arrangement. This position is intended for individuals who understand the risks of an early-stage startup, are comfortable with uncertain funding timelines, and are motivated by the opportunity to build something substantial while participating in its long-term ownership and success.

Ole Ole is located in beautiful Austin Texas, however, this role requires some travel we are privately held and rapidly growing!

What We’re Building

OleOle is building a global digital platform dedicated to football, bringing together social networking, messaging, live scores, content, commerce, and a new ecosystem of Mini Programs.

Our ambition is to create a platform serving 400 million football fans worldwide, with an ecosystem of 2 million professional football teams, brands, businesses, and developers creating Mini Programs that operate directly within OleOle.

Mini Programs are central to this vision.

Rather than requiring users to download separate applications, OleOle will enable businesses, football clubs, and independent developers to build lightweight, integrated applications that run within the OleOle ecosystem.

A football club could create a Mini Program for merchandise, memberships, ticketing, or exclusive fan experiences. A global brand could create interactive campaigns, product experiences, or customer services. Independent developers could build applications for commerce, entertainment, travel, utilities, and other services.

These Mini Programs will share a common foundation for identity, authentication, payments, permissions, discovery, and integration with the broader OleOle platform.

Our objective is not simply to introduce another application feature. We are building a developer ecosystem and application platform within OleOle, enabling millions of businesses and developers to create services that can reach a global audience without requiring users to leave the platform.

We are looking for an exceptional architect who can design the technical foundations of this ecosystem from the ground up.

OleOle — Where Fans Kick Off.

jobs.title: Backend Engineer
jobs.excerpt: About Jan Jan is an open source AI assistant built by Menlo.
jobs.description:
About Jan

Jan is an open source AI assistant built by Menlo. It began as a private, offline alternative to ChatGPT and has grown into a general purpose agent that runs open models locally on your own hardware, or connects to frontier models like GPT, Claude, and Gemini when you want them. Give Jan a task and it works on its own until the job is done. Built in public around one belief: AI should be open, private, and answer only to you.

The Role

We are building Jan Router, an enterprise LLM gateway. Think OpenRouter, but for organizations: one gateway in front of many model providers that routes traffic intelligently and gives an org a single place to manage keys, budgets, quotas, usage, and billing. You will bootstrap it from scratch and own the architecture, the first production deploy, and everything from the request proxy to the billing ledger. This is a lean, agent-native setup. Rather than leaning on a large team, you will orchestrate coding and execution agents to ship at team-scale velocity, while keeping the hard backend judgment to build a billing-grade gateway that does not fall over. The router is your primary charge, but not your only one: you will also contribute to the Jan Agent, wiring agent and tool traffic through the same routing, metering, and controls. You are fluent in trade-offs. You know which parts can ship fast and be hardened later, and which parts, like the money path and auth, have to be right the first time. This role suits a Backend or Software Engineer ready to open a new chapter: working closely with a frontier research team and building real AI services from the bottom up, starting at the model level.

What You'll Do

  • Build the core gateway: a unified, OpenAI-compatible API in front of multiple providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, plus self-hosted and OSS models).

  • Own provider routing and reliability: load balancing, automatic failover, and cost and latency-aware routing.

  • Build billing and metering that is correct, not approximate: per-request token accounting, usage ledgers, cost attribution per team, user, and key, budgets, and spend limits.

  • Ship org controls: API key management, per-team and per-user quotas, rate limiting, and RBAC.

  • Handle streaming and performance: low-overhead proxying, streaming responses, connection handling, and caching where it helps.

  • Contribute to the Jan Agent and connect it to the router: route its model and tool calls through the gateway, and make agent traffic first-class in metering, controls, and observability.

  • Make deliberate speed-versus-correctness calls: move fast where iteration is cheap, refuse to cut corners where a bug means a bad charge or a leaked key, and pay down debt on your own initiative.

What We Look For

  • Work agent-natively as your default, running multiple agents in parallel, pushing token throughput hard, with your own review and guardrail discipline, using open harnesses like Pi, Hermes Agent, and OpenCode as your daily drivers, on open and frontier models alike.

  • Acquainted with LLM API systems: providers, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, streaming, tool calling, and token accounting.

  • Experience with LLM infra: inference proxies, provider SDKs, token counting, or existing gateways and routing services (LiteLLM, cliproxyapi, 9router, Omnirouter, and similar) as reference points.

  • Acquainted with core AI concepts: context windows, inference, prompting, evals, and how open models differ from hosted providers in practice.

  • Proven ability to ship from zero to production and own the result, including infra, deploy, alerting, and CI/CD, regardless of which stack you did it in.

  • Open-minded and pragmatic: you weigh speed against correctness case by case, hold strong opinions loosely, and change course when the evidence says so, all while staying fast-moving and comfortable with full ownership and ambiguity.

Nice to Have

  • A track record building production backend services that handle real traffic: APIs, auth, data modeling, deploy, and monitoring.

  • Experience with payments, billing, metering, or usage-based systems, or the rigor to build them correctly (idempotency, reconciliation, no dropped or double charges).

  • Comfort with high-throughput proxying, gateways, and streaming, and the performance concerns that come with them.

  • Solid datastore skills: PostgreSQL, Redis, queues where needed, and sound schema design for usage and billing data.

  • Strong in at least one of TypeScript or Python.

  • Comfort with Docker, Kubernetes, OAuth and OIDC, API keys, RBAC, tenant isolation, and secure secrets handling.

  • Familiarity with the ecosystem or other OSS LLM tooling.

  • MCP and tool-calling knowledge, directly relevant since you will help the router carry the Jan Agent's agent and tool traffic.

  • Go or Rust for high-performance proxying, not required.

  • Contributions to open agent tooling or harnesses: a Pi extension, a Hermes skill, an OpenCode plugin, or anything in the open-models ecosystem we can look at.

Why Join Menlo

Jan is open-source, built in public, and already in the hands of millions. You will own a real product end to end, work shoulder to shoulder with a frontier research team, drive agents hard to ship at a pace a traditional team cannot match, and set the bar for how a lean, agent-native backend gets built. If you want to be in the arena shipping something that matters, this is the place.

A Note on AI

You don't need deep AI expertise for every role, but we do expect everyone at Menlo to be intellectually curious, drawn to tinkering and discovery, and excited to use AI as a real collaborator in their work. For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement. When that's the case, we'll say so explicitly in the qualifications. People who thrive here don't treat AI as a novelty. They use it to think better, and make their work easier for others to build on.

Equal Opportunity and Accommodations

We hire talented people from a wide range of backgrounds. If you're excited about a role but don't meet every bullet, we still encourage you to apply. Menlo Research is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any legally protected characteristic. Menlo provides reasonable accommodations during the application process. If you need one, please let your recruiter know.

jobs.description:
Contract | Remote, worldwide | $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location | 10-20 hrs/week

Please note that eligibility may vary depending on your location, as some regions may not be supported by the client.

Check out this Loom video for more details:

We're looking for highly experienced software engineer (SR+) to help evaluate the quality of interactions with modern coding agents such as OpenAI Codex and Claude Code.

This is not a traditional engineering role. You won't be writing production code. You'll be evaluating something harder: whether the model thinks like a great engineer.

What this role actually is

You will assess how AI coding agents behave in real-world scenarios, focusing on:

• Whether the response makes sense

  • Whether the preamble and reasoning are useful
  • Whether the output reflects strong engineering judgment
  • Whether the interaction feels right to an experienced developer

This role is about engineering taste. Syntax correctness is the easy part.

What you'll be doing

  • Evaluate AI-generated coding interactions end to end
  • Judge whether outputs are useful, correct at a high level, and aligned with how a strong engineer would think
  • Assess the quality of explanations and reasoning, not just the code
  • Distinguish between levels of response quality (what makes something a 2 vs a 4)
  • Give clear, opinionated feedback in writing on what worked, what didn't, and what felt off or misleading
  • Help define what great looks like when working with tools like Cursor, Codex and Claude Code

What we mean by "taste"

We're looking for engineers who can answer questions like:

  • Does this feel like something a strong engineer would actually say?
  • Is this explanation helpful, or just technically correct?
  • Is the model guiding the user well, or just dumping output?
  • Would this interaction build or erode trust?

You should be comfortable making subjective but rigorous judgments, and explaining them clearly.

Who you are

  • Senior, Staff or Principal-level engineer (or equivalent experience)
  • Strong background in TypeScript/JavaScript or Python
  • Hands-on experience with at least one of OpenAI Codex, Claude Code or Cursor
  • Deep familiarity with modern AI-assisted dev workflows
  • Able to evaluate code without executing it or reviewing every line
  • Strong written and spoken English (B2 or above). You'll be writing detailed feedback and recording short video explanations, so this is a hard requirement
  • Comfortable giving direct, opinionated feedback
  • High bar for what good engineering looks like

Nice to have

  • Prior exposure to prompt design or evaluation workflows
  • Experience mentoring senior engineers or defining engineering standards

Engagement details

  • Rate: $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location

• Hours: 10-20 hours/week, flexible

  • Duration: ongoing. Projects run from about two weeks to a few months each, and we offer new ones to evaluators who do well
  • Start: as soon as you clear the take-home and a project has an open seat
  • Process: one take-home evaluation exercise with a recorded Loom walkthrough. No interview

The Principal Quality Engineer provides strategic advice and guidance to functional team(s). Highly skilled with broad, advanced technical experience.

Humana is committed to helping people achieve their best health by delivering innovative technology solutions that power exceptional member, provider, and associate experiences.


The Principal, Quality Engineering is a senior individual contributor and hands-on technical leader responsible for advancing modern, AI-focused quality engineering practices across Humana’s software delivery ecosystem. This role defines, demonstrates, and scales what good looks like for enterprise quality engineering across the SDLC through technical expertise, reference patterns, automation frameworks, quality intelligence, and practical implementation guidance.


This role serves as a deeply technical expert in AI-enabled quality engineering, test automation, quality architecture, engineering excellence, and continuous quality practices. The Principal partners closely with the core EQE Platform team, Quality Engineering Segements, Product, Engineering, Architecture, Enterprise Engineering Enablement, Agile teams, DevOps, Cybersecurity, Risk, Compliance, Audit, and Data/AI teams to embed scalable, secure, measurable quality practices into delivery workflows, release processes, engineering platforms, and operational support models.


This is a hands-on principal role, not a people management role. The Principal will accelerate Humana’s enterprise quality engineering transformation by building reusable solutions, creating technical standards and exemplars, coaching teams directly, and ensuring responsible use of AI across quality engineering processes. This role is also responsible for defining and operationalizing what good looks like for EQE across the SDLC, including test strategies and approaches, release management, incident tracking, production validation, and continuous improvement.


Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Quality Engineering Strategy, Standards, and Technical Leadership

  • Define, refine, and operationalize enterprise quality engineering standards, patterns, reference architectures, and technical guidance across software delivery teams.
  • Define and continuously evolve what good looks like for Enterprise Quality Engineering across the full SDLC, including planning, development, testing, release, deployment, production validation, support, and continuous improvement.
  • Establish practical, reusable best practices for embedding quality engineering into each SDLC phase, including requirements quality, test planning, test design, automation strategy, validation, release readiness, production verification, and supportability.
  • Create and maintain reusable frameworks, starter kits, accelerators, example implementations, and practical guidance for quality planning, test automation, regression strategy, API and UI testing, service virtualization, code quality, deployment validation, performance and resilience testing, release readiness, observability-driven quality, production validation, and AI-assisted quality engineering.
  • Define enterprise quality expectations, guardrails, and example patterns that help teams consistently apply EQE best practices within Agile, DevOps, and platform-based delivery models.
  • Create technical guidance for quality-related Definition of Done expectations and quality checkpoints across delivery workflows to improve consistency, traceability, and readiness.

  • Partner with engineering enablement and platform teams to ensure quality practices are reflected in enterprise tooling, templates, reusable workflows, and CI/CD pipeline patterns.

Hands-On AI-Focused Quality Engineering

  • Lead the practical application of AI-enabled quality engineering capabilities across the SDLC through hands-on experimentation, prototyping, implementation, and refinement.
  • Design and implement patterns for responsible use of AI in quality engineering, including test case generation, test data analysis, requirements analysis, defect clustering and triage, risk-based testing, code review support, automation acceleration, quality intelligence, and production issue analysis.
  • Evaluate and pilot generative AI, machine learning, intelligent automation, and analytics solutions that improve test effectiveness, speed, coverage, defect prevention, and engineering productivity.
  • Develop guardrails, technical recommendations, and implementation patterns for safe and responsible use of AI-enabled engineering tools in partnership with Data/AI, Cybersecurity, Risk, Compliance, and Legal stakeholders.
  • Build proof of concepts, reference implementations, and engineering patterns that demonstrate measurable value from AI-enabled quality practices.
  • Help teams integrate AI-assisted workflows into daily engineering practices while preserving human oversight, traceability, quality, and compliance expectations.

Test Automation, Quality Architecture, and Engineering Excellence

  • Define what good looks like for test strategies and test approaches across product, platform, integration, API, UI, data, performance, resilience, security-aligned, and operational validation scenarios.
  • Establish enterprise guidance for selecting appropriate test levels, test types, coverage models, and automation approaches based on risk, architecture, criticality, and delivery context.
  • Create patterns for modern test strategy development that incorporate risk-based testing, non-functional validation, test data management, and environment strategy.
  • Standardize quality engineering approaches for unit, integration, system, acceptance, migration, infrastructure, data, and deployment validation testing to improve consistency and delivery confidence.
  • Define measurable expectations for automation maintainability, reliability, execution efficiency, evidence quality, and test coverage effectiveness.
  • Design scalable approaches for validating APIs, services, event-driven systems, data workflows, web applications, and platform integrations.
  • Establish automation patterns that support shift-left and shift-right quality practices, including pre-merge validation, deployment validation, synthetic testing, and production verification.
  • Promote engineering practices that strengthen quality outcomes, including clean code practices, atomic commits, meaningful pull requests, code quality controls, and automated quality gates.

Governance, Risk, Compliance, and Quality Maturity

  • Contribute deep technical expertise to enterprise Quality Engineering governance frameworks, standards adoption models, and maturity assessments.
  • Define what good looks like for EQE controls and evidence across SDLC governance requirements, including traceability, standards adherence, test management, quality metrics, release readiness, and production validation support.
  • Translate enterprise SDLC standards and governance expectations into actionable quality engineering practices that teams can implement consistently and with minimal friction.
  • Help define maturity criteria for SDLC quality adoption, release quality discipline, incident learning integration, and test strategy effectiveness across teams.
  • Define measurable quality criteria, engineering controls, and evidence expectations aligned with SDLC governance and regulatory requirements.
  • Partner with Risk, Compliance, Cybersecurity, Audit, and AI governance stakeholders to ensure quality engineering practices align with enterprise policies, control expectations, and responsible AI principles.
  • Identify quality, control, and process risks in software delivery workflows and recommend pragmatic improvements that reduce friction while strengthening compliance.

Quality Intelligence, Metrics, and Insight

  • Define and implement actionable quality metrics and telemetry that help teams improve engineering quality, delivery confidence, release readiness, and production outcomes.
  • Define measurable indicators for what good looks like across SDLC quality adoption, release quality, incident quality signals, defect escape trends, and test strategy effectiveness.
  • Establish dashboards and scorecards that help teams assess adherence to EQE best practices in areas such as test planning, release readiness, incident learning, automation effectiveness, and quality outcomes.
  • Partner with platform, DevOps, engineering, and data teams to create dashboards and scorecards for automation coverage, defect trends, test reliability, release quality, deployment validation, code quality, pipeline health, DORA-aligned indicators, and AI-enabled quality outcomes.
  • Use quality, release, and incident data to identify systemic issues, bottlenecks, and improvement opportunities across teams and platforms.
  • Translate engineering and quality signals into recommendations that improve reliability, maintainability, speed, and production performance.

Enablement, Coaching, and Enterprise Influence

  • Provide expert-level coaching and hands-on guidance to engineering and quality teams adopting modern and AI-enabled quality engineering practices.

The Cybersecurity Security Compliance Manager leads day-to-day delivery of cybersecurity compliance programs and assessment workstreams for clients operating within the Defense Industrial Base (DIB), federal marketplace, and regulated commercial environments. This role bridges strategic direction from the Senior Manager (ML6) and hands-on execution by Senior Consultants and Consultants. The Manager is accountable for delivery quality, schedule adherence, team performance, and client satisfaction at the workstream or program level.

Engagements will span CMMC Level 1 and Level 2 certification readiness and assessment support, FedRAMP authorization packages (Moderate and High baselines), NIST Risk Management Framework (RMF) implementations, and security assessment and authorization (A&A) programs across Products industry clients — with initial demand concentrated in Aerospace & Defense and other highly regulated sectors.

The Manager interfaces directly with client program managers, Information System Security Officers (ISSOs), CISOs, and IT leadership, translating complex compliance requirements into practical delivery plans and guiding clients through regulatory processes with clarity and measurable progress.

What You'll Do:


• Manage end-to-end delivery of CMMC, FedRAMP, and NIST RMF compliance workstreams — including assessment planning, evidence collection coordination, gap analysis, remediation tracking, and documentation review through completion

• Develop and maintain detailed delivery plans, milestone schedules, resource assignments, and RACI matrices aligned to client program timelines and C3PAO or agency assessment deadlines

• Lead client-facing workshops, technical working sessions, status briefings, and executive readouts — communicating progress, risks, and decisions clearly to program and senior leadership

• Guide clients through CMMC Level 1 and Level 2 scoping — including CUI identification, in-scope asset definition, assessment boundary documentation, and C3PAO engagement preparation

• Oversee development and quality review of core compliance artifacts — System Security Plans (SSPs), Security Assessment Reports (SARs), Plans of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms), authorization packages, and Control Implementation Summary (CIS) documents

• Coordinate directly with client ISSOs, Information System Security Managers (ISSMs), system owners, and technical SMEs to resolve compliance issues and maintain program momentum

• Support FedRAMP boundary definition, system characterization, and authorization package development — including Agency and JAB authorization path activities

• Identify, document, and manage program risks, issues, and dependencies — escalating material issues to the Senior Manager with recommended resolution approaches

• Review and approve deliverables produced by Senior Consultants, and Consultant for technical accuracy, quality, and alignment to engagement standards

• Mentor junior team members, providing technical coaching on CMMC practices, NIST SP 800-53 and SP 800-171 control frameworks, FedRAMP documentation requirements, and A&A methodology

• Contribute to proposal development, solution scoping, and staffing model design for new or expanding compliance engagements

• Develop reusable delivery accelerators, assessment templates, and methodology documentation that strengthen and scale the Security Compliance practice


Travel may be required for this role. The amount of travel will vary from 25% to 100% depending on business need and client requirements.

Here's What You Need:


  • Minimum of 5 years of relevant cybersecurity experience, including a minimum of 2 years in a role with direct project, workstream, or team leadership accountability in a client-facing or delivery context — experience must include planning, managing, and delivering complex work products, not solely technical or individual contributor activitie
  • Minimum of 5 years of direct, hands-on experience supporting cybersecurity compliance, assessment, or authorization programs involving one or more of the following: CMMC (Level 1 or Level 2), FedRAMP (Moderate or High baseline), NIST SP 800-53, NIST SP 800-171, or NIST Risk Management Framework (RMF) — general NIST CSF awareness alone does not satisfy this requirement
  • Minimum of 5 years experience in a relevant Products industry environment (Aerospace & Defense, Consumer Goods, Life Sciences, Industrial, or similarly regulated sector) with demonstrated understanding of industry-specific regulatory requirements, compliance drivers, and client operating environments
  • Minimum of 5 years demonstrated ability to develop and execute delivery plans, manage risks and issues, maintain delivery quality, and communicate status across complex, multi-stakeholder engagements
  • Minimum of 5 years working knowledge of CMMC scoping guidance, CMMC Practice requirements (Levels 1 and 2), and the Cyber AB ecosystem — including the roles of OSCs, C3PAOs, RPOs, Registered Practitioners (RPs), and Registered Practitioner Advanced (RPA) within the CMMC certification and advisory landscape
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent (minimum 12 years work experience; Associate's Degree + minimum 6 years work experience)

Preferred Qualifications:


  • Familiarity with federal cybersecurity policy — including DFARS 252.204-7012, FISMA, CUI handling requirements (32 CFR Part 2002), and OMB guidance applicable to contractor and agency compliance obligations
  • CMMC Registered Practitioner Advanced (RPA) — issued by the Cyber AB, reflecting advanced training and formal registration as a senior CMMC advisor and implementation specialist; or CMMC Certified Assessor (CCA) for candidates with an assessment-focused background
  • CMMC Registered Practitioner (RP) — entry-level Cyber AB practitioner credential, demonstrating formal CMMC advisory training; considered if RPA or CCA not yet obtained
  • CISSP, CISA, CRISC, CGRC, or equivalent senior professional certification
  • FedRAMP authorization support experience — including package component development (SSP, SAP, SAR, CIS, CRM) and direct experience with Agency or JAB authorization workflows
  • DoD and Defense Industrial Base (DIB) sector experience — including familiarity with CMMC implementation across prime contractors and supply chains, DFARS clause compliance, and CUI safeguarding obligations
  • Experience with GRC and compliance management platforms such as Archer, ServiceNow GRC, ZenGRC, Drata, Vanta, or equivalent evidence management and program tracking tools
  • Proficiency with Microsoft 365 (Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint, Teams) and project or task tracking tools (Jira, Azure DevOps, Planner, or similar)
  • AI security experience where it relates to compliance automation, AI-assisted evidence analysis, risk identification, or secure AI adoption in regulated program environments
  • Strong executive communication skills — able to present complex compliance topics clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences at client senior leadership and C-suite levels
  • Prior consulting or professional services experience in a client-facing delivery role

jobs.description:
Job Title:

Lead Site Reliability Engineer - Bilingual

Job Description

We're Concentrix. The intelligent transformation partner. Solution-focused. Tech-powered. Intelligence-fueled.

The global technology and services leader that powers the world’s best brands, today and into the future. We’re solution-focused, tech-powered, intelligence-fueled. With unique data and insights, deep industry expertise, and advanced technology solutions, we’re the intelligent transformation partner that powers a world that works, helping companies become refreshingly simple to work, interact, and transact with. We shape new game-changing careers in over 70 countries, attracting the best talent.

In our Information Technology and Global Security team, you will deliver the latest technology infrastructure, transformative software solutions and industry-leading global security for our staff and clients. You will work with the best in the world to design, implement and strategize IT, security, application development, innovation, and solutions in today’s hyperconnected world. You will be part of the technology team that is core to our vision of develop, build and run the future of Integrated Services.

Our game-changers around the world have devoted their careers to ensuring every relationship is exceptional. And we’re proud to be recognized with awards such as "World's Best Workplaces," “Best Companies for Career Growth,” and “Best Company Culture,” year after year.

We embrace our game-changers with open arms, people from diverse backgrounds, who are curious and willing to learn. Your natural talent to help others and go beyond WOW for our customers will fit right in with what we do and who we are.

Join us and be part of this journey towards greater opportunities and brighter futures.

As a Lead Site Reliability Engineer, you’ll play a strategic role in shaping and scaling our DevSecOps ecosystem. You’ll lead the design and implementation of automated CI/CD pipelines, enforce enterprise-grade security and compliance standards, and drive reliability across the software delivery lifecycle.


In this role, you’ll partner closely with development, operations, and platform teams to define best practices, optimize deployment workflows, and ensure applications are resilient, observable, secure, and continuously improving. Your expertise will help accelerate innovation while maintaining high standards for quality, performance, and operational excellence.


Responsibilities

  • Work with key technology stakeholders to deliver SRE strategies and capabilities that drive and support the digital transformation agenda.
  • Design, build, and maintain cloud-native CI/CD workflows using tools such as GitHub Actions, Jenkins, or ArgoCD.
  • Automate build, test, and deployment processes for microservices across Kubernetes clusters and multi-cloud environments.
  • Integrate security into every stage of the delivery pipeline, including automated vulnerability scans, secrets management, and policy enforcement using tools such as Snyk, HashiCorp Vault, and OPA.
  • Build fault-tolerant systems using cloud-native patterns such as self-healing, auto-scaling, and blue/green deployments.
  • Leverage Kubernetes, service meshes, and distributed tracing to maintain application performance, resilience, and uptime.
  • Deploy and manage observability stacks such as Prometheus, Grafana, ELK, and OpenTelemetry to monitor system health.
  • Define SLOs, SLIs, and error budgets; establish intelligent alerting; and lead incident response and postmortem practices.
  • Use Terraform and cloud vendor tools to provision, manage, and optimize cloud resources.
  • Maintain version-controlled infrastructure and enforce effective change management practices.
  • Ensure systems meet regulatory and organizational standards, including SOC 2, HIPAA, and ISO 27001.
  • Automate audit trails and implement continuous compliance checks to support governance requirements.
  • Partner with developers, QA, operations, and platform engineers to embed reliability and security throughout the SDLC.
  • Advocate for cloud-native best practices and drive adoption of scalable, secure, and resilient engineering patterns.
  • Guide junior engineers, conduct technical reviews, and foster a culture of ownership, automation, and continuous learning.
  • Identify performance bottlenecks, reduce toil through automation, and evolve infrastructure and processes to support rapid innovation and growth.
  • Complete all assigned, mandatory training within the timeframe provided.
  • Conduct and/or participate in regularly scheduled 1:1 meetings with your direct manager and/or direct reports.

Qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience in Site Reliability Engineering, platform engineering, or a related discipline.
  • Strong experience defining and managing SLOs, SLIs, and error budgets.
  • Demonstrated experience with incident management, blameless postmortems, and reliability improvement practices.
  • Hands-on experience with observability tooling such as Prometheus, Grafana, and OpenTelemetry.
  • Experience working with cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or GCP.
  • Strong knowledge of Kubernetes and containerized environments.
  • Proficiency in scripting or programming languages such as Python, Go, or Bash.
  • AI-native mindset with experience using AI tooling to support engineering productivity, automation, reliability, or operational excellence.
  • Experience with chaos engineering tools or practices such as Chaos Monkey, Gremlin, or LitmusChaos preferred.
  • Experience with Infrastructure as Code tools such as Terraform or Pulumi preferred.
  • Familiarity with DevSecOps practices and security tooling preferred.
  • Experience with GitOps workflows and CI/CD pipelines preferred.
  • Strong collaboration skills with the ability to influence engineering teams and technology stakeholders.
  • A continuous improvement mindset with a passion for automation, resilience, security, and scalable systems.

We’re looking for an experienced software engineer to take our products to the next level. The ideal candidate will have a strong technical background and be able to work independently to design, develop, and implement new features and functionality. They will also be able to troubleshoot and resolve issues with existing code. Additionally, they will be responsible for mentoring and training junior software engineers. The most successful candidate will be a self-starter with a passion for software engineering and a willingness to learn new technologies.

  • Engage with the development team in active problem solving to identify technical roadblocks and recommend solutions that can improve the direction of our products

  • Help improve software engineering practices across the development team and be an advocate of a culture of quality code development including writing/maintaining technical documentation

  • Take technical responsibility for features or subsystems of our products, working with minimal supervision to deliver high-quality and stable software

  • Understand testing & integration methodologies (continuous integration, continuous delivery, unit vs. integration tests). Be able to write and maintain your own automated tests

  • Handle short term and long term projects concurrently and adjust on-the-fly as priorities change

  • Handle rapidly changing requirements without losing sight of the “big picture”

  • Balance the need for speed and stability – we move fast, but we don’t sacrifice quality

  • Maintain a sense of urgency and drive issues to closure

  • Communicate effectively (written and verbal) with both technical and non-technical staff at all levels of the organization

  • Proactively share knowledge with others on the team

  • Take initiative to learn new technologies and keep up-to-date with industry trends

  • Help mentor junior engineers and contribute to their professional development

Required Skills and Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science or related field

  • 5+ years professional experience as a software engineer

  • Expertise in Java, C++, or other programming languages

  • Experience with Agile development methodology

  • Strong problem-solving skills

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills

Preferred Skills and Qualifications

  • Master’s degree in computer science or related field

  • 7+ years professional experience as a software engineer

  • Experience leading a team of engineers

  • Experience with cloud computing platforms, such as AWS or Azure

  • Knowledge of DevOps practices

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer
jobs.excerpt: We are an AI-first company building innovative agentic frameworks, the systems that let LLM-driven agents research, plan, and act reliably in production.
jobs.description:
We are an AI-first company building innovative agentic frameworks, the systems that let LLM-driven agents research, plan, and act reliably in production. That means orchestrating multi-step workflows with retries, skips, and parallel execution; keeping long-running work persistent and observable; and serving per-tenant retrieval at scale. This isn't about wrapping an LLM in an API call, it's the hard backend engineering that makes agents dependable.

Our stack is Python (FastAPI) on AWS, with Terraform. We hire on engineering depth and judgment, not on a keyword count, and we work in whichever language you're strongest in during the interview (more below). As a Senior Engineer, you will own backend services and the orchestration layer on top of them, from design through deployment, operation, and the on-call that follows.

Our team is based in Tehran and pays salaries monthly in USD.

What You Will Do:

  • Design, build, and own backend services and the agent-orchestration layer end to end.

  • Build resilient systems that stay correct under load and degrade gracefully when a model, tool, or dependency fails.

  • Ensure operational excellence by making long-running, multi-step work observable and debuggable in production.

  • Shape technical direction through rigorous code reviews, mentorship, and pushing back on specifications when they misalign with engineering reality.

  • Drive the full software development lifecycle, translating ambiguous requirements into durable architectures and actionable technical plans.

What We Are Looking For:

  • 5+ years building and operating production backend systems, with deep ownership of at least one non-trivial service you can talk through end to end.

  • Deep fluency in your primary backend language, and the ability to pick up a new one fast. We work in Python; if it is not your daily language today, we expect you to ramp quickly.

  • Strong systems fundamentals — concurrency, data modeling, and failure modes — and the judgment to choose the right abstraction rather than the cleverest one.

  • Sound reasoning under ambiguity: you ask the clarifying question first, make the trade-offs explicit, and adapt when the constraints change.

  • Solid grasp of infrastructure and operations, including message brokers (Kafka, RabbitMQ), SQL and NoSQL stores, and running services in containers with an orchestrator (Kubernetes, ECS, Nomad, or similar).

  • Professional written English, enabling you to write crisp design documents and align stakeholders on complex technical trade-offs.

Even Better:

  • AWS (especially ECS) and Terraform, or comparable cloud and Infrastructure-as-Code experience.

  • Hands-on work with LLM, agentic, or RAG systems (LangChain, CrewAI, OpenAI/Anthropic SDKs, Hugging Face) and a real grasp of how non-deterministic agent steps differ from ordinary functions.

  • A recognized-bar engineering background, owned open-source work, or another verifiable standout signal.

How We Hire:

We use a deliberate, transparent two-stage process designed to see how you think and build:

  • 1. A 120-minute conversation focusing on your background and a collaborative system-design exercise and cultural fit..

  • 2. A 120-minute live technical session involving code review, live coding, and a self-review.

You may complete the technical session in your strongest language (Python, Go, Java, Kotlin, PHP, or TypeScript/Node.js). Web search is encouraged; AI assistants are not used. We want to see your fundamental engineering judgment.

What We Offer:

  • Competitive USD-based salary and a comprehensive benefits package.

  • Hybrid work flexibility with hours that support deep work.

  • The opportunity to work at the frontier of agentic AI, tackling hard problems with high ownership.

  • A highly educated, agile senior team that values pragmatism, learning, and continuous improvement.

If you would rather be judged on how you think than on a buzzword list, we would like to talk!
